entry.title: SD-LoRA: Distilling Structural Knowledge into LoRA During Training for Few-Shot Vision-Language Adaptation
entry.summary: SD-LoRA: Training-Time Structural Distillation into LoRA for Few-Shot Vision-Language Adaptation arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper presents SD-LoRA, a method for adapting vision-language models like CLIP to tasks with very few labeled examples. During training, it uses a graph model over high-resolution image tokens and text to capture fine-grained structural relations, then transfers this knowledge into a lightweight LoRA-adapted CLIP model. The graph is discarded at inference, which needs only one CLIP-LoRA forward pass and a cache-based classifier. The authors report accuracy gains over a strong CLIP-LoRA baseline across 11 few-shot benchmarks. ★★★★ Notable: The authors distill a training-only token graph teacher into LoRA and discard it at inference, reporting 1.8–3.0 point gains over CLIP-LoRA across 11 few-shot benchmarks.

entry.title: Adversarial Multiplicity: How Chosen Models Can Be Used to Steer Predictions
entry.summary: Adversarial Multiplicity: Cherry-Picked Models and the Limits of Disclosure arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies predictive multiplicity, where similarly accurate models disagree on individual predictions, and how parties can exploit this to steer outcomes. It distinguishes soft manipulation through innocuous model choices from hard manipulation through direct parameter edits. The authors find that flexible models can be manipulated to reverse individual predictions with minimal performance loss while passing black-box audits. entry.title: Where Long-Video QA Gains Come From: A Controlled Audit of Frame Selection, Evidence Injection and Model Routing
entry.summary: Where Do Reported Long-Video QA Gains Come From? A Controlled Audit of Frame Selection, Evidence Injection, and Expert Routing arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper introduces VideoRouteAudit, a controlled evaluation that varies one decision at a time, comparing frame selection, injecting non-visual evidence, and routing to another answering model while keeping the rest fixed. On the full Video-MME long-video subset (900 questions, 8 frames), no tested frame selector significantly beat uniform sampling. The authors also show that results on the commonly used 200-item subsets are unstable, and they correct errors in their own earlier results. Code and scripts are publicly released. ★★★★ Notable: The authors audit frame selection, evidence injection, and answering-model routing separately under controlled conditions; on Video-MME long videos, no selector significantly beats uniform sampling.

entry.title: Recursive Sparse Attention: Long-Context Modeling at Logarithmic Cost
entry.summary: Recursive Sparse Attention: Million-Token Length Extrapolation at Logarithmic Cost arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper proposes RecSA (Recursive Sparse Attention), which organizes the KV cache into a tree where each node is summarized by one key and one mean-pooled value, so each query costs O(log L) to select and read. The model is initialized from Qwen3-4B and trained on 0.62B tokens at the original 32K training length. On RULER, RecSA outperforms all baselines at every length from 131K to 2M, scoring 60.5 at 1M compared with 40.0 for the best baseline, Dense + DCA. With optimized kernels, it is faster than dense attention in end-to-end prefill and decoding from 64K to 2M tokens. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a recursive tree over the KV cache with shared poolers, cutting selection cost to O(log L), and report RULER gains from 131K to 2M tokens, scoring 60.5 at 1M.

entry.title: SAFE-Teen: Testing Chatbot Safety in Teen Mental Health Chats
entry.summary: SAFE-Teen: Evaluating Chatbot Safety Across Adolescent Mental Health Conversations arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper evaluates how AI chatbots handle simulated conversations with adolescents aged 13-17 on mental health and related topics. Across 32,555 conversations with 18 chatbot APIs and 22 safety criteria, the overall failure rate was 43.3% without a teen-aware system prompt and 24.9% with one. When teens pushed back on chatbot answers, failures on diagnosis, medication, and substance misuse boundaries rose by 10-12 percentage points without the prompt, for more than 80% of chatbots. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report evaluating 18 chatbot APIs across 32,555 simulated teen conversations, comparing how teen pushback changes safety failure rates.

entry.title: Compositional Unalignment: Auditing Safety in Vision-Language Models
entry.summary: Compositional Unalignment: Auditing Safety in Large Vision-Language Models arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper studies how large vision-language models can produce harmful outputs when an image and a prompt that are harmless separately are combined. It finds that minimal supervised fine-tuning reaches benchmark scores similar to a multi-stage reinforcement-learning pipeline, so such scores alone do not show robust safety. The authors propose CMaG, a training-free method that reduces compositional safety scores by up to 65 points on Qwen2.5-VL-7B and LLaVA-1.5-7B while keeping over 98% of outputs coherent. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose training-free CMaG, showing recognition and refusal of compositional harm are decoupled; experiments on two 7B LVLMs report large safety score drops.

entry.title: SeVerus: A Gamified Benchmark for Rust Verification Agents
entry.summary: SeVerus: Context-Aware, Gamified Benchmarking for Rust Verification arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper presents SeVerus, a method for generating benchmarks for Verus, a verifier for Rust programs, where each verification target becomes a gamified quest. Its levels progressively remove supporting proof lemmas, from requiring only one missing lemma up to proving the target with none. Applied to six open-source Verus projects, it produced 819 quests with 10,095 levels. Experiments with several coding agents show success declining and cost rising as proof context is withdrawn. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report a gamified, context-withdrawal method for building Verus benchmarks, evaluated on 819 quests across six open-source projects with several coding agents.

entry.title: Multi-step SWE: Can Coding Agents Keep Building on Their Own Code?
entry.summary: Multi-step SWE: Can Coding Agents Keep Building on Their Own Code Over Long Horizons? arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper introduces Multi-step SWE, a benchmark of 69 software engineering tasks, each a chain of 5 to 15 dependent steps on one codebase. Every step starts from the code the agent produced in earlier steps, so early decisions and errors carry forward. The tasks span four engineering families and nine languages. Among nine frontier models, the best solve rate is 18.5%, and 38 of the 69 tasks are unsolved by any model. ★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce a 69-task, nine-language benchmark of chained coding steps; the best of nine frontier models reports only an 18.5% solve rate.

entry.title: A Night at the LLM Zoo: Flow Matching for Generating Pretrained LLM Weights
entry.summary: A Night at the LLM Zoo: Data Conditioned Flow Matching for Generating Pretrained LLM Weights arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The authors build a population of GPT-2 language models, varying the training data mixture across web text, books, mathematics, coding, and French. They train a flow matching model conditioned on the data mixture to generate complete pretrained model weights in a compressed weight space. The generator produces models for unseen data mixtures that perform similarly to the models in the original population. ★★★★ Notable: The authors condition flow matching on data mixtures to generate full GPT-2 weights, reporting zero-shot generalization to held-out mixtures across a 300-model zoo.

entry.title: Exact polynomial-time computation of proper equilibria in two-player zero-sum extensive-form games
entry.summary: Polynomial-Time Computation of Extensive-Form Proper Equilibria in Two-Player Zero-Sum Games arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper presents a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm that computes an exact extensive-form proper equilibrium in finite two-player zero-sum games with perfect recall and rational data. Each information set is assigned a geometric permutahedron of allowable action probabilities, which is embedded in a polynomial-size sequence-form polytope via a scaled doubly stochastic representation. The authors use sign stability of a parametric linear system to obtain an exact rather than approximate equilibrium, and the resulting probabilities are rational with polynomial encoding length. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report a deterministic polynomial-time exact algorithm for extensive-form proper equilibria in two-player zero-sum games, using geometric permutahedra and doubly stochastic embeddings; imp

entry.title: Optimistic Hedge in Games: How Much Regret It Can Avoid
entry.summary: Optimistic Hedge in General-Sum Games: Fundamental Limits and Regret Bounds via Temporal Approximation arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies Optimistic Hedge, a learning method that updates weights multiplicatively with one step of extrapolation, and how much regret it incurs in general-sum games. The authors show that in two-player games some learning rate gives regret of O(n log n) independent of the number of rounds. In games with three or more players, they construct games where some player's regret grows exponentially in the number of actions. Their upper bound comes from a temporal approximation framework that also gives a simpler proof of a known bound for m-player games. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show two-player games admit horizon-independent regret O(n log n), while three-player games have exponential lower bounds, using a temporal approximation framework.

entry.title: Shaping and Monitoring Models via Internal Representations
entry.summary: Shaping & Monitoring Models through their Internal Representations arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper proposes Mechanistic Shaping, a training framework that steers models through their internal representations so they avoid specified concepts in outputs and in the features used for decisions, such as harmful content or gender in résumé screening. Experiments across vision, medical imaging, and language, with models up to 32B parameters and several training methods, show targeted behaviors are substantially reduced while task performance is preserved. The authors also introduce a hierarchy of monitors and identify three ways shaped concepts can evade them, finding that shaped concepts largely remain monitorable. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose Mechanistic Shaping, a unified framework, report reduced targeted behaviors across vision, medical, and language tasks up to 32B, and characterize three circumvention mechanisms.

entry.title: FFMT: Frequency-Factorized Multi-Rate Tokenization for Generating Dance from Music
entry.summary: FFMT: Frequency-Factorized Multi-Rate Tokenization for Music-to-Dance Generation arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper proposes FFMT, a method that splits dance motion into a low-frequency choreographic scaffold and a high-frequency residual for tokenization. The two components use different token rates and codebook sizes, and generation proceeds in two stages, with coarse choreography planned first and local details articulated afterward. Experiments on AIST++ and FineDance show strong distributional fidelity, realistic diversity, and music-motion synchronization, and ablations support the frequency factorization design.

entry.title: Designing video clips with cinematic language through human-AI collaboration
entry.summary: Designing with Cinematic Language: An Intent-Driven Approach to Human-AI Video Clip Co-Creation arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper presents CineAssist, a human-AI co-creation system that treats cinematic language as an interactive design medium linking creative intentions to executable video controls. The authors built a Cinematic Language Design Space and an annotated dataset from 107 filmmaking sources and 1,436 film clips. The system combines a multi-agent workflow, an interactive cinematic editor, and a preference learner, and three studies evaluate its usability, cinematic quality, and preference evolution.

entry.title: When Preferences Clash with Scores: Diagnosing and Correcting Constraint Drift in DPO
entry.summary: When Scores Conflict with Preferences: Pre-Alignment Diagnosis and Adaptive Correction of Constraint Drift in DPO arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) when pairwise preferences disagree with pointwise criteria such as length, correctness, or safety scores. The authors show that conflict pairs, where the preferred output scores worse, tend to increase constraint cost, while matching pairs tend to repair it, so the net effect depends on their balance. They introduce a closed-form pre-alignment diagnostic, ρ*_eq, computed from dataset statistics, and propose Conflict-aware DPO (CoDPO), which down-weights conflict pairs and adds an adaptive margin shift. Across four domains, CoDPO reduces drift while largely preserving vanilla DPO's preference learning.

entry.title: Multi-UAV cooperative deep semantic autoencoders designed for communication networks
entry.summary: Design of Multi-UAV Cooperative Deep Semantic Autoencoders for Communication Networks arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper proposes MC-DSA, a multi-UAV cooperative deep semantic autoencoder for communication networks operating under bandwidth constraints. The system uses one task UAV and several support UAVs that cooperate through semantic communication to improve efficiency and data processing. Support UAVs establish links only when the semantic similarity between their local images and the task query exceeds a threshold, reducing redundant transmissions. Experiments report improved image semantic segmentation accuracy and maintained task execution efficiency compared with benchmarks.

entry.title: EnvOpt: Automatically Optimizing the Environments Where AI Agents Work
entry.summary: EnvOpt: Automated Optimization for Agent Environments arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper proposes optimizing the stationary environments in which LLM agents operate, such as a company's shared Slack workspace or data sources, alongside model parameters and harnesses. The method, EnvOpt, works end-to-end without graders or reference answers, using real or synthetic tasks. On AutomationBench, it cut Claude Haiku 4.5's cost by 72.7% and raised its pass rate by 14.34%.

entry.title: Test-Time Self-Play: Improving Model Reasoning Without a Verifier
entry.summary: Test-Time Self-Play: Scaling without a Verifier arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper introduces Test-Time Self-Play (TTSP), a method that uses asymmetric self-play to scale a language model's compute at deployment without needing a verifier to check answers. On a difficulty-calibrated subset of LiveCodeBench v6, TTSP performs best at every verifier strength tested, and its advantage over the strongest baseline grows as the verifier weakens. In the no-verifier limit, it achieves a 35% absolute improvement in mean@8, though gains disappear when the base policy almost never produces the correct answer.

entry.title: Neural network method for solving high-dimensional high-field kinetic equations under uncertainty
entry.summary: Asymptotic-Preserving Tensor Neural Networks for 3D High-Field Kinetic Equations with Applications to Uncertainty Quantification arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper proposes an asymptotic-preserving tensor neural network (APTNN) for solving high-dimensional, multiscale kinetic equations used in plasma and semiconductor simulations. It uses a canonical polyadic decomposition to cut computational and memory costs, and adds a first-moment equation to the loss to improve accuracy in the high-field limit. Numerical results show that for a 3D3V VPFP problem with multiple random inputs, training takes under 30 minutes on a single GPU.

entry.title: Acoustic Anomaly Detection for Early Spotting of Drill Jamming
entry.summary: Acoustic Anomaly Detection for Early Identification of Drill Jamming arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper proposes a system that uses ultrasonic sensors to detect acoustic warning patterns before drill jamming occurs in CNC machining. The authors release a public dataset of time- and frequency-domain acoustic features from 17 drills. They compare a semi-supervised autoencoder with supervised XGBoost using Leave-One-Drill-Out validation, finding the autoencoder achieves a Recall of 1.00, a consolidated F1-score of 0.81, and an AUC of 0.8294.

entry.title: MIKU: A framework for standardized, physically consistent PBR material generation
entry.summary: MIKU: Material Invariance and Knowledge Unification for PBR Generation arXiv · Nov 5, 2026MIKU is a unified framework that standardizes PBR asset representation and generates physically consistent materials for 3D content. It normalizes heterogeneous material parameterizations into a common space and standardizes the pipeline from preprocessing to texture synthesis. A two-stage multi-view diffusion approach first generates geometry-aware albedo maps, then predicts roughness and metallic maps conditioned on them. The authors report state-of-the-art texture quality and semantic consistency across object parts.

entry.title: Rethinking how LoRA adjusts its rank, from what is used to what is missing
entry.summary: From What Is Used to What Is Missing: Rethinking Dynamic Rank in LoRA arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies how the rank of LoRA, a parameter-efficient fine-tuning method, should change during training. The authors show that the unobservable subspace of standard factor gradients coincides with the normal space of the low-rank manifold, so gradients alone cannot tell under-optimization from task-relevant directions outside the current space. They propose GEAR, which combines tangent-space optimization, normal-spectrum estimation, and geometric initialization to evolve the rank, and report the best average performance across language and vision benchmarks.

entry.title: AtlasULP: Domain-aware universal link prediction using a relation atlas
entry.summary: AtlasULP: Domain-aware Universal Link Prediction via Relation Atlas arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper proposes AtlasULP, a framework for universal link prediction that aims to make predictions on arbitrary unseen graphs without training separately for each one. It uses a relation atlas to capture structural associations between node pairs from both global and local perspectives. Building on this, it introduces a domain-guided prompting model that generates domain-aware prompt tokens and performs in-context link prediction. The authors report that AtlasULP consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods across diverse graph domains.

entry.title: Selective Retrieval Routing for Repairing Knowledge Graphs with Multiple Violations
entry.summary: Selective Retrieval Routing for Multi-Violation Knowledge Graph Repair arXiv · Nov 5, 2026Knowledge graphs often contain missing or inconsistent facts that undermine applications built on them. The paper proposes a framework for iterative graph repair in which an LLM repair agent edits the graph while a router decides whether it may access a researcher agent that retrieves external evidence. The authors extend a violation-injection framework to generate cases with multiple compatible violations and known reference repairs, and use the agent's outcomes to train the router. Across six evaluation suites on two building-automation datasets, the router uses fewer repair-time tokens than always enabling retrieval and achieves higher repair F1 than always disabling it in five of the six suites.

entry.title: Convergence of the final iterate in stochastic gradient methods without bounded assumptions
entry.summary: Last-Iterate Convergence of Stochastic Gradient Methods for Unbounded Problems arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies whether stochastic gradient methods converge when the last iterate is used, without assuming bounded domains or bounded variance. Black-box variational inference is used as a running example. Under two related relaxed variance assumptions, the authors show a near-optimal anytime rate of order O~(1/√T) for the last iterate. When the horizon T is known, the logarithmic factor is removed, giving the optimal order O(1/√T), which matches results under bounded variance or bounded domain assumptions.

entry.title: Permanent and Transient Representations for Continual RL: Two Complementary Systems Balancing Stability and Adaptation
entry.summary: Permanent and Transient Representations for Continual Reinforcement Learning arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper addresses the stability-plasticity trade-off in continual reinforcement learning, where agents must retain prior knowledge while adapting quickly to new situations. Building on Anand & Precup (2023), it uses complementary learning systems, pairing parametric representations for long-term learning with non-parametric representations for transient, situation-specific adaptation. The authors introduce a novel non-parametric approximation for estimating the transient value function in complex tasks. Experiments show the method enables online learning and outperforms competitive baselines on image-based tasks and Craftax-Classic.

entry.title: Rethinking Data Selection: Coverage Over Difficulty in LLM Fine-Tuning
entry.summary: Rethinking Data Selection: The Importance of Coverage over Difficulty in LLM Fine-Tuning arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper examines how to select training data for fine-tuning large language models to reduce computation cost. The authors find that difficulty-based selection methods often fail to beat random selection for LLM fine-tuning, because random selection better represents the input space, giving it better coverage. They propose a simple clustering-based method that prioritizes coverage, which matches or exceeds random selection on diverse single-domain tasks and outperforms all compared methods on the multi-domain Tülu 3 mixture.

entry.title: WeightLoop: Programming Neural Network Weights Using Experimental Feedback
entry.summary: WeightLoop: Weight-Space Programming with Experimental Feedback arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper introduces WeightLoop, a framework that turns experimental feedback into persistent updates to deployed predictive models. A language model first writes a bounded, reusable parameter-editing program, which, as new measurements arrive, identifies prediction discrepancies, validates candidate edits against observed outcomes, and writes the selected changes back to the original model. In offline replay, targeted edits improved mean ranking utility over random edits in seven of eight endpoint-budget settings.

entry.title: Take It From Here: Evaluating Coding Agents on Taking Over Software Projects
entry.summary: Take It From Here: Evaluating Coding Agents On Project Takeover arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper studies whether coding agents can take over long-term projects by recovering applicable requirements from interaction history and updating them for new requests. Across six model-harness configurations and 37 validated targets, the mean complete-delivery rate with full history is only 4.95%. The authors introduce ReqMemBench, which combines requirement diagnostics with delivery validation to evaluate project takeover.

entry.title: ArtiVidRM: A verifiable reward model that scores AI-generated videos by listing visible flaws
entry.summary: ArtiVidRM: Verifiable Artifact-as-Rubric Reward Modeling for Explicit Quality Articulation in Video Generation arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper presents ArtiVidRM, a reward model for judging the quality of AI-generated videos. It first identifies visible generation artifacts and organizes them into a structured list, then uses these artifacts as explicit rubrics for scoring. A multi-reward reinforcement learning strategy jointly optimizes artifact prediction and quality assessment. The authors report state-of-the-art results on video preference benchmarks.

entry.title: Ranking Port Impacts from Tropical Cyclones with a Two-Stage System
entry.summary: Robust Ranking of Port Impacts from Impending Tropical Cyclones: A Two-Stage Recommendation System arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper proposes a two-stage recommendation framework that estimates which ports a tropical cyclone is likely to affect and for how long. The first stage selects candidate ports by proximity to the expected landfall location, and the second stage ranks them by estimated impact days. Using AIS-derived data for 37 Gulf of Mexico ports and 31 cyclones, the authors compare ranking models, and Wide & Deep Learning shows the closest agreement with observed rankings in tests on Hurricanes Nicole and Ian.

entry.title: Provably efficient representation learning for constrained MDPs with low-rank structure
entry.summary: Provably Efficient Representation Learning for Low-Rank CMDPs arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies representation learning in low-rank Constrained Markov Decision Processes, aiming to maximize cumulative rewards while satisfying constraints on cumulative utility. The authors propose MFRLC, a model-free algorithm combining LSVI-UCB with primal-dual techniques, which learns the mapping from representations to value functions without explicitly estimating the transition kernel. The paper proves that MFRLC achieves reward regret and constraint violation of order K^{3/4} with high probability, independent of the state space size.

entry.title: Householder Motion Embedding: a noise modulation method for controllable motion in video generation
entry.summary: Householder Motion Embedding: Noise Modulation for Motion-Controllable Video Generation arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper proposes Householder Motion Embedding (HME), a method that encodes user-specified motion signals into diffusion noise for video generation. It applies a sequence of Householder reflections as an orthogonal transformation to each location's channel vector, preserving the per-frame Gaussian structure while adding cross-frame correlations. Experiments reportedly match or outperform state-of-the-art methods and run 2.7 times faster than noise warping.

entry.title: How Transformers Learn Low-Level Control from Context Alone
entry.summary: How do Transformers Perform Low-Level Control In-Context? arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies whether Transformer neural networks can control unstable nonlinear systems, the cartpole and two-link acrobot, using only a context trajectory of the unforced system dynamics, without knowing its parameters. The authors use a GPT-2-style multi-head architecture and identify training techniques essential for learning low-level control, with expert trajectories used only during training. Analysis across checkpoints shows in-context control is possible and policy performance generally improves as context length grows. The models also generalize to stabilize systems outside the training distribution.

entry.title: How Should Agents See Code? Rethinking Code Representations for Agentic Software Engineering
entry.summary: How Should Agents See Code? Rethinking Code Representations for Agentic Software Engineering arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies how map-based code representations, including abstract syntax trees, call graphs, module dependencies, documentation-enriched search, and a hybrid of these, affect LLM agents on repository-level software engineering tasks. Compared with a raw-file tool baseline on LinuxFLBench, SWE-bench Pro, SecBench, and SWT-bench, the workflows reduce token usage in several settings. Their effect on task success varies by task, so the benefits are not universal.

entry.title: How Language Models Encode Singular and Plural Grammar
entry.summary: Encoding and Propagation of Grammatical Number in Large Language Models arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper uses sparse autoencoders (SAEs) to examine how a small 70-million-parameter language model (Pythia-70M) represents subject-verb number agreement. The authors identify features for plural nouns, plural subjects, and generating plural verbs, and show that removing them makes the model produce singular verbs instead. Singular-related features were less effective, and similar results were reported for Gemma-2-2b and Llama-3.1-8b.

entry.title: Generating Synthetic Rare Market Scenarios with Multimodal Latent Diffusion
entry.summary: Scenario Augmentation for Rare Financial Events via Multimodal Latent Diffusion arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper addresses the scarcity of extreme market movements by generating synthetic samples with a multimodal latent diffusion model. Each market window is represented through structured market variables, a spatial image transformation, and a portfolio return sequence, with variational autoencoders producing compact latent codes and a class-conditional diffusion model learning their joint distribution. Conditional Value-at-Risk defines rare windows and guides generation toward the minority regime. On U.S. technology equities across four window lengths, the synthetic samples outperform tabular diffusion baselines in fidelity and support, and an XGBoost classifier trained on real and generated data reaches AUCs of 0.953 to 0.960.

entry.title: Graph neural networks for power allocation in vehicular sensing-and-communication systems
entry.summary: Graph Neural Networks for Resource Allocation in Integrated Sensing and Communication arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies vehicles that share a limited power budget between sensing targets and communication receivers in integrated sensing and communication networks. It proposes GNN-ISAC, a graph neural network power allocation method that distinguishes inter-provider interference edges from intra-provider power-sharing edges and is trained without labels using a sensing-penalized sum-rate loss. Simulations show communication sum-rates close to the WMMSE algorithm, low sensing-link violation rates, much lower computation, and generalization to larger networks without retraining.

entry.title: Efficient fine-tuning of diffusion robot policies via latent noise representation bridging
entry.summary: Efficient Diffusion Policy Fine Tuning with Latent Noise Representation Bridging arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper addresses the high cost, low sample efficiency, and lack of theoretical guarantees when reinforcement learning is used to adapt pre-trained diffusion and flow policies for robotics. It introduces the Latent Noise Linear Markov Decision Process (LNL-MDP) and a Bridge Equation that resolves the noise aliasing problem by aligning noise-space and action-space values through a shared representation. Based on this, the authors propose LARBRID, an algorithm that learns this representation to optimize the initial noise distribution, and report up to 2-3x performance gains on robotic locomotion and manipulation tasks.

entry.title: Satisficing as competitive Bayesian weighting: a minimal model of goal-directed choice
entry.summary: Satisficing as competitive Bayesian weighting: a minimal model of goal-directed choice under an unattained target arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies how animals and humans choose relative to goals (aspiration levels) that are not yet met. It introduces Risk-sensitive Satisficing (RS), a bandit learning rule, and shows it can be rewritten as an estimator called Attention Competitive Bayes (ACB), where the aspiration level is each action's prior mean and the trial budget limits how far evidence can override it. In Bernoulli bandit simulations, adjusting the aspiration level from evidence reduced regret.

entry.title: How Far Back Must a Model Look? A 30-Year Time-Context Study for Colorectal Cancer Prediction from Primary-Care Records
entry.summary: How Deep is the Signal? Time-Context up to 30 Years for Colorectal Cancer Prediction in a Primary-Care EHR Model arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper examines how far back in time an EHR prediction model must look to capture its earliest predictive signal. The authors pretrained a decoder-only transformer on 1.4 billion coded events from 3.6 million primary-care patients in North West London, then fine-tuned it to predict colorectal cancer with a 12-month pre-diagnostic buffer. Evaluated on 1,008 cases and 9,582 matched controls, discrimination improved from an AUROC of 0.551 at 2 years to 0.590 at 18 years and then plateaued, with about 80% of the gain reached within 10 years.

entry.title: Measuring and Optimizing Energy Use of TinyML on Small Embedded Devices: A Systematic Mapping Study
entry.summary: Energy Measurement and Optimization of TinyML in Resource-Constrained Embedded Systems: A Systematic Mapping Study arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper maps existing research on energy-aware TinyML, machine learning run on microcontrollers and other resource-limited devices. It identifies the common models and learning approaches, classifies energy evaluation methods and metrics, and examines technical factors that affect energy consumption. The reported optimization techniques are organized into a structured taxonomy. The authors note limited standardization in experimental platforms, measurement procedures, and reporting, which restricts reproducibility and direct comparison.

entry.title: HyFlash: A Prefix-Memory Prior for On-Device Speculative Decoding (a paper on a compact parallel drafter that speeds up text generation on devices)
entry.summary: HyFlash: A Prefix-Memory Prior for On-Device Speculative Decoding arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper proposes HyFlash, a compact parallel drafter that speeds up speculative decoding on devices. It adds a prefix-memory prior that uses local attention for recent context and draft-position interactions, and recurrent memory that compresses historical target features into fixed-size states. Experiments show that HyFlash achieves higher acceptance than full-context attention while using substantially less KV storage, with larger gains for shallow drafters and long contexts.

entry.title: Reweighting Can Backfire: How Dataset Traits Shape a Fairness Method's Effects
entry.summary: Reweighting is not Harmless: Understanding the Role of Dataset Characteristics arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies reweighting, a data pre-processing method that assigns different weights to training points to promote fairer model behavior. Using controlled simulations that vary group size and baseline event prevalence across 3,000 datasets, the authors find that reweighting narrows between-group gaps in positive classification and false negative rates, but partly by reducing positive classifications and raising false negative rates for the higher-prevalence group. The pattern appears across six classifiers while overall accuracy barely changes.

entry.title: Adaptive k for Nearest Neighbors via Genetic Algorithm
entry.summary: Evolutionary Adaptive Neighborhood Learning: A Genetic Algorithm for Instance-Dependent k Optimization in Nearest Neighbor Classification arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper proposes EANK, a method that tunes the number of neighbours in k-nearest neighbour classification. Instead of one global k, it assigns each instance an adaptive k based on local descriptors such as density and label entropy. A genetic algorithm optimizes this neighbourhood policy. Experiments on synthetic data and twelve public datasets show competitive results against tuned global-k baselines under nested cross-validation.

entry.title: TriAttention: A unified sparse mixed-precision attention method for faster long-context LLM inference
entry.summary: TriAttention: Unified Sparse Mixed-Precision Attention for Long-Context LLM Inference arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper introduces TriAttention, which assigns query-key tiles in attention to skipping, 4-bit, or 8-bit computation to reduce inference cost. Each head's computation regions are encoded with two diagonal-distance boundaries, chosen through offline calibration and a model-wide allocator under a shared budget. A fused kernel runs during prefill, and the compressed key-value cache is reused during decoding. The authors report generation speedups of up to 7.88x over Torch attention and 2.65x over a BF16 baseline, with quality comparable to the original models on general and long-context tasks.

entry.title: Using Transformers to speed up turning evolved agent neural networks into readable symbolic rules for teaching and learning
entry.summary: Using Transformers for Teaching and Learning via Symbolic Distillation of Neural A-life Agents arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper addresses how neural networks that control artificial-life agents, which evolve over generations, can be distilled into compact symbolic policies that humans can interpret. Such symbolic policies also let agents share knowledge efficiently across a population. The authors propose using a transformer pre-trained on random percept-action data to speed up this distillation, with the transformer architecture derived through neural architecture search. Experiments compare distillation methods and examine how the symbolic space affects population dynamics through self-reflection and teaching and learning.

entry.title: Linking information-theoretic empowerment and capability-based human power through goal revelation
entry.summary: Goal Revelation as a Bridge Between Information-Theoretic Empowerment and Capability-Based Human Power arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper addresses power in AI safety, proposing two formal measures: information-theoretic empowerment and capability-based individual power. Using Fano's inequality, the authors derive a lower bound from individual power on goal revelation, the mutual information between a human's latent goal and the realised trajectory, and chain it to empowerment. It also identifies failure modes where maximising empowerment or revelation can mislead an assistant. Simulations in random environments show the three quantities are correlated but not interchangeable.

entry.title: KG-Neighbor: Building Neighborhoods for Embedding Plots with Knowledge Graphs
entry.summary: KG-Neighbor: Knowledge-Guided Neighborhood Construction for Embedding Visualization arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper proposes KGN, a method that represents each instance's relational knowledge as knowledge graph triples and uses shared triples as semantic evidence to adjust embedding distances and rebuild top-k neighborhood graphs, without using class labels. It also introduces IDProfile (IDP) to assess whether residual mismatches are supported by the source content or reflect projection failures. Across eight text and image dataset-encoder conditions, KGN's maximum NMI and LT_2D exceed the kNN baseline in every condition.

entry.title: MAC-v2: Long-horizon model-based value expansion from pixels
entry.summary: MAC-v2: Long-horizon model-based value expansion from pixels arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies whether long-horizon model-based value expansion works in pixel-based offline reinforcement learning. It introduces MAC-v2, which uses a reconstruction-free latent world model and action chunking to enable such expansion from pixels. Across visual benchmarks including visual OGBench, MMBench2, Robomimic, and LIBERO-10, MAC-v2 reportedly outperforms model-free and model-based offline RL baselines.

entry.title: $D^2$-OPD: Separating Direction and Distance in Extrapolative On-Policy Distillation
entry.summary: D²-OPD: Separating Direction and Distance in Extrapolative On-Policy Distillation arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper proposes $D^2$-OPD, a method that improves extrapolative on-policy distillation by decoupling how far the learning target moves from the direction it moves in. A per-prefix hard KL constraint limits the target's distance from the teacher, while an adaptive mix of the teacher's post-training shift and the initial student-teacher gap sets the direction. The student is optimized with forward KL. On mathematical reasoning benchmarks across three settings, it achieves the highest score, outperforming the strongest baseline by up to 9.45 points, and ablations confirm each component's contribution.

entry.title: How AI Agents Waste Tokens: A Unified Framework for Measuring Waste
entry.summary: How Do AI Agents Waste Your Money? arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper introduces a unified framework for measuring token waste across different AI agent systems. It records and normalizes complete agent trajectories, uses an LLM-as-a-Judge to identify removable text spans, and maps them back to the original trajectory for token-level measurement. In online pruning experiments on two distinct agent benchmarks, the authors removed 41-46% of the model's reasoning while largely preserving task performance.

entry.title: Archetypal contexts in language model neurons: a possible architecture for intelligence
entry.summary: Archetypal contexts in the neurons of language models: an architecture for intelligence? arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper tests inside the model Qwen3.8-27B whether relational patterns such as "tipping point" are stored separately from the subject domains where they appear. Silencing the neurons for a pattern stops the model from recognizing it while it still identifies the topic, and silencing topic neurons has the reverse effect. The authors report a layered structure in which languages, topics and archetypes sit in separate layers, and they propose this as the mechanism behind analogy and intelligence. The neurons, texts and code are released for reproduction.

entry.title: Compressing Neural Networks by Choosing Among Equivalent Parameter Forms
entry.summary: Neural Compression over Equivalence Classes: Exact Gauges and Functional Rate-Distortion arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper observes that the same or nearly the same neural network function can be written with many different parameter vectors, while deployment usually stores only the one produced by training. The authors use this representational freedom for compression, searching over exact function-preserving transformations and controlled functional perturbations while keeping the existing compressor unchanged. On SmolLM2 and Qwen3, checkpoint size under Zstandard compression falls by up to 23.4%, with similar relative reductions under gzip, Brotli, and ZipNN.

entry.title: Source-balanced Capped Fisher: Bounded Evidence Aggregation for Language Model User Inference
entry.summary: Source-balanced Capped Fisher: Bounded Evidence Aggregation for User Inference in Language Models arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper addresses user inference, which asks whether a data source contributed documents to a language model update when only fresh documents from that source are observed. The authors propose source-balanced capped Fisher (SCF), which uses known nonparticipating sources to measure how unusual each document score is, caps individual contributions, and averages them within each source. Experiments on four real-world datasets show SCF achieves the highest AUROC among evaluated aggregation methods in four domains, with competitive detection power and false-positive rates generally near or below nominal levels.

entry.title: Loopback Transformer: A Unified Look at Residual Looped Transformers
entry.summary: Loopback Transformer: Towards a Unified View of Residual Looped Transformers arXiv · Nov 5, 2026Looped Transformers cut parameter counts by repeatedly applying shared blocks, but how repeated results are reused depends on more than sharing. The paper analyzes how residual connections store and reread block outputs, and proposes the Loopback Transformer, which uses geometric decay to set total update weight and attention to allocate it. On ClimbMix, it reaches lower validation loss than standard Transformers using 40-75% of their Transformer parameters, and scores higher mean accuracy on thirteen downstream tasks at 1.4B and 3B.

entry.title: TileQuant: Tile-Level Mixed-Precision Post-Training Quantization for LLMs
entry.summary: TileQuant: Tile as the Precision-Allocation Unit for LLM Mixed-Precision Post-Training Quantization arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper presents TileQuant, a training-free post-training quantization framework for large language models that assigns precision to hardware-aligned 2D weight tiles rather than whole columns. Within each projection's retention budget, the highest-scoring tiles stay at 16-bit and the rest use 8-bit, with scores derived from offline calibration. The authors report 2.66x the original model's generation throughput and preserved quality across language modeling, reasoning, long-context retrieval, and question answering tasks.

entry.title: Using fractional physics-informed neural networks to model how social media posts go viral
entry.summary: Fractional physics-informed neural networks to model social media virality arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper presents a fractional physics-informed neural network that learns the memory effects and nonlinear growth of social media engagement, then uses symbolic regression to express these dynamics as interpretable equations. Tested on 348 posts from X (formerly Twitter), splitting the 24-hour window into four segments substantially improved reconstruction. The segmented model reconstructed 64% of held-out trajectories within a mean squared error of 0.01, compared with 44% for the best of nine classical baselines.

entry.title: Canonical Correlation Neural Networks: Neural networks using in-view and cross-view covariances as structural priors
entry.summary: Canonical Correlation Neural Networks arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper introduces Canonical Correlation Neural Networks (CANEs), which use in-view and cross-view covariance matrices as relational inductive biases for multi-view data. Spectral analysis draws analogies to Canonical Correlation Analysis (CCA), but CANEs are trained directly on downstream tasks. The authors bound output error under finite-sample covariance perturbations, showing dependence on controllable Lipschitz constants of learned filters rather than the singular-value gap that governs CCA. Experiments on seven brain imaging and motion sensing datasets show CANEs match or outperform single-view, two-view, and CCA-based baselines, often with fewer parameters.

entry.title: Task-calibrated random features that cancel task-relevant sampling errors
entry.summary: Task-Calibrated Random Features via Influence-Based Error Cancellation arXiv · Nov 5, 2026Random features approximate kernel integrals with Monte Carlo sampling, but only some frequency-sampling errors affect a downstream task. The paper proposes Task-Calibrated Random Features (TCRF), which balance frequency moments built from task-specific influence using shared weights, yielding a reusable calibration space. Paired experiments show better approximation to exact kernel ridge regression at larger frequency budgets and to the exact empirical Stein discrepancy under a fixed alternative. Gains are smaller with cross-validated ridge, and near the Stein null, extra ordinary frequencies are preferable.

entry.title: Structured Machine Theory of Mind: Explaining and Counterfactually Analyzing Agent Behavior via Editable Belief and Desire Representations
entry.summary: Structured Machine Theory of Mind from Agent Trajectories arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper introduces Structured Machine Theory of Mind (SMToM), a framework that attributes explicit belief and desire representations from observed trajectories within a Belief-Desire-Intention causal structure. The resulting model, BDIBottleneck, is tested in a controlled pedestrian navigation domain and outperforms trajectory-only and unsupervised-context neural baselines. Counterfactual interventions on inferred beliefs and desires are shown to shift predicted destinations as expected.

entry.title: TrustMix: Keeping Pretrained Models Reliable When Data Shifts
entry.summary: TrustMix: Graceful Degradation for Pretrained Models under Distribution Shift arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper introduces TrustMix, a lightweight post-hoc method that blends a pretrained model's predictions with a user-specified fallback distribution. As the measured out-of-distribution deviation grows, predictions move toward the fallback, so performance degrades gracefully instead of failing abruptly. The method needs no retraining and is tested on tabular, image, and language tasks. The authors report improved uncertainty under distribution shift and show it can serve as a surrogate for Bayesian optimisation.

entry.title: τ-bench-LILT: Testing Chatbots on Realistic Multilingual Tool Tasks
entry.summary: τ-bench-LILT: Evaluating Conversational Agents on Realistic Multilingual Tool-Use Tasks arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper presents τ-bench-LILT, a multilingual extension of τ³-bench covering German, Korean, Turkish, and Farsi across airline, retail, telecom, and banking domains. Every layer of the benchmark is localized, including customer databases, user-simulator prompts, and tasks. Evaluating eight agent models, the authors find the largest performance drops compared to English in Korean and Farsi retail, up to 61 points in pass^4.

entry.title: Comparing Adapter Designs After EEG Pretraining Under Matched Parameter Budgets
entry.summary: Backbone-Informed Adaptation after EEG Pretraining: A Capacity-Controlled Study arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies how to adapt EEG foundation models to downstream tasks after pretraining. It compares a backbone-informed (native) adapter against a token-wise multilayer perceptron that transforms each feature vector independently, with roughly matched trainable parameter counts and a frozen pretrained encoder. Experiments cover emotion recognition, sleep staging, and EEG event classification across two backbones. The native adapter shows no consistent advantage, and the relative performance depends on the backbone, task, and training protocol.

entry.title: MammoSeek: A mammography agent that zooms selectively to produce grounded reports
entry.summary: MammoSeek: A Mammography Agent with selective zooming for grounded reports arXiv · Nov 5, 2026MammoSeek is a mammography agent that mimics how radiologists read screening mammograms: it forms a global impression, then selectively magnifies suspicious candidate regions at full resolution. Guided by a BI-RADS assessment skill, it assigns a category and generates a localized, structured report for each breast, and combines this with image-model scores to decide on recall. On the EMBED and VinDr-Mammo datasets it reaches exam-level AUCs of 0.824 and 0.818, and selective zooming outperforms both no zooming and forced zooming.

entry.title: VINO: A new 3D scene representation learning method using Volume Transformers
entry.summary: VINO: Revisiting 3D Representation Learning with Volume Transformers arXiv · Nov 5, 2026Self-supervised learning has produced vision foundation models for images, but 3D scene representation learning has lagged behind. This paper revisits current 3D methods and replaces the common hierarchical PTv3 backbone with a ViT-like Volume Transformer. It also redesigns the cross-view matching and masked prediction objectives, and shifts 2D-to-3D distillation to view-consistent supervision. The resulting framework, VINO, learns label-free 3D scene representations that substantially improve dense linear probing on indoor and outdoor benchmarks and transfer well to out-of-domain settings.

entry.title: ShapleyOG: Fast Adaptive Shapley Value Estimation Using Odd Gaussian Processes
entry.summary: ShapleyOG: Fast Adaptive Shapley Value Estimation with Odd Gaussian Processes arXiv · Nov 5, 2026Shapley values are a common tool for explaining machine learning predictions, but exact computation is infeasible, so they are estimated from a limited number of evaluations. This paper introduces ShapleyOG, which exploits the fact that Shapley values depend only on the odd component of the game, allowing a Gaussian process surrogate to be fitted on that component alone with half as many observations. It also refits the surrogate on a sparse schedule and efficiently updates the coalition selection criterion in between. The authors report that ShapleyOG matches the accuracy of ShaplEIG while reducing its overhead by up to three orders of magnitude.

entry.title: Meta-Frieren: a two-stage framework for online learning that picks agent-environment pairs to maximize reward
entry.summary: Meta-Frieren: Beyond Single Level Online Learning arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies a two-stage online optimization problem in which a meta-learner first selects an agent-environment pair each round, and the chosen agent then interacts with the environment to earn a reward. The authors introduce Meta-Frieren, a general framework for maximizing cumulative reward, built on a UCB-style selection criterion. Experiments support the theoretical results and show its application to hyperparameter optimization across several model classes.

entry.title: A conditional independence test based on neural quantile resolution
entry.summary: Structural Conditional Independence Test via Neural Quantile Resolution arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper proposes QRCIT, a conditional independence test that compares P(X|Z) and P(X|Y,Z) through a quantile deformation learned by a residual quantile-flow model. It yields a global predictive-gain statistic calibrated by conditional randomization and an inspectable deformation field over context and quantile level. The authors also introduce the Structural Dependency Benchmark (SDB) of dependence patterns motivated by real applications. QRCIT improves detection of structured alternatives on synthetic PNL and SDB benchmarks and performs competitively on Sachs, METABRIC, and CCLE/PLX4720 data.

entry.title: A survey of nonlinear filtering for data assimilation and new generative-AI score filters
entry.summary: A Survey of Nonlinear Filtering Methods for Data Assimilation and Recent Advances in Generative AI-Enabled Score Filters arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This survey reviews nonlinear filtering methods used in data assimilation, which combines models with noisy observations to estimate system states. It notes that Kalman, particle, and kernel-based approaches each face limits with nonlinear, non-Gaussian, or high-dimensional chaotic systems. The paper traces the mathematical foundations of the Ensemble Score Filter (EnSF), which encodes the filtering density in a score function estimated by a training-free Monte Carlo method. It also examines fourteen extensions of EnSF, twelve of which keep this core estimator.

entry.title: Depth or Description? One-step latent scores as alternatives to lookahead in proactive information acquisition
entry.summary: Depth or Description? When a One-Step Latent Score Replaces Lookahead in Proactive Information Acquisition arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies how a proactive agent should decide which questions to ask before acting. Exact lookahead evaluates combinations of questions but is expensive and relies on a fitted model, while a cheap one-step score can miss such combinations. The authors find that the need for deep search depends on how the hidden cause is described: a one-step score on the label can overlook interactions among answers, whereas a score on a suitable latent cause does not. When that latent encodes the decision, it can replace most of the deep search at a fraction of the cost.

entry.title: FastAFD: When Splitting Attention and Expert Compute Pays Off on NVLink Racks
entry.summary: FastAFD: When Does Attention-FFN Disaggregation Pay on Rack-Scale NVLink? arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper presents FastAFD, an engine that separates attention from mixture-of-experts (MoE) layers on GB200 NVL72 systems and overlaps computation across microbatches. Compared with the best vLLM wide expert-parallel setting, it reaches up to 1.17x throughput on Qwen3 and 1.16x on Qwen3.5, and matches it on MiniMax-M2.5. The authors also provide an analytical model that predicts AFD throughput within 3% using only profiles from colocated vLLM.

entry.title: Perceptual distortion for overfitted video coding with sliced spatial matching and temporally aligned errors
entry.summary: Perceptual Distortion for Overfitted Video Coding: Sliced Matching in Space, Error Alignment in Time arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper proposes a perceptual distortion framework for overfitted video codecs. Spatially, it introduces a local sliced Wasserstein distortion that matches feature distributions through one-dimensional optimal transport, capturing cross-channel dependencies without enforcing exact alignment. Temporally, it uses a flow residual that constrains coding errors along motion trajectories to preserve consistency. On UVG and HEVC Class B with the COOL-CHIC codec, it reduces BD-rate by 9.2% in DISTS and 3.0% in LPIPS versus frame-wise WD, and lowers tOF by 10.2% at matched rate.

entry.title: Do More AI Agents Make a System More Reliable? A Study of Multi-Agent LLM Reliability
entry.summary: More Agents, More Reliable? System-Level Reliability of Multi-Agent LLMs under Operational-Profile Uncertainty arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper examines whether software built from several cooperating large language model agents is actually more reliable than a single model. The authors combine HIP-LLM, a hierarchical imprecise-probability method for assessing single LLMs, with a Bayesian network modeling the system's failure logic, propagating failure-probability intervals into a reliability envelope. In a pipeline extracting regulated chemical-hazard statements, majority voting over three models protected against the weakest model but did not clearly exceed the best one. The authors conclude that adding agents yields a more defensible reliability claim, but not automatically a more reliable system.

entry.title: Matriarchy Classics: A Method for Swapping Only the Gendered Words in Classic Novels
entry.summary: Matriarchy Classics: A Computational Approach to Swap Only Gendered Words in Classic Novels arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper presents a computational method for gender-swapping public domain novels that programmatically guarantees only gendered words are changed. The authors demonstrate it on two novels, transforming Pride and Prejudice into a matriarchal Regency England and The Great Gatsby into a matriarchal Jazz Age. They suggest such gender-swapped novels could help investigate gender biases among readers, authors, societies, and AI systems.

entry.title: Context-aware automated NMR structure elucidation using chemical precursors as added input
entry.summary: Context-Aware Automated NMR Structure Elucidation arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper proposes a protocol that combines AI-based spectroscopic structure elucidation with chemical context such as known reactants or a desired product. Automated retrosynthetic analysis is used to generate large training sets of molecules paired with synthetic precursors. When the context is informative, Top-15 accuracy reaches up to 95.4%, and even uncorrelated context yields accuracy comparable to the original NMR framework.

entry.title: A Method Using Proxy Variables to Measure Racial Disparities in Text-to-Image Models
entry.summary: A Proxy-Based Method for Measuring Racial Disparities in~Text-to-Image~Generators arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper presents an automated method for auditing text-to-image generators for racial bias against demographic benchmarks. It adapts racial proxy variables from U.S. antidiscrimination law, classifies generated images by race, and compares the results with public census data, while also measuring skin tone and image similarity. Experiments on three models using geographic, occupational, and surname proxies show notable variation across models and proxy categories. For example, Imagen 4 Fast overrepresents white-classified images and produces lighter, more homogeneous skin tones.

entry.title: Teaching Agents Behavioral Principles Instead of Rewards: A New Reinforcement Learning Approach
entry.summary: Teaching Agents the "Principle", Not the "Reward" arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper argues that reward-based reinforcement learning forces agents to infer designers' intent from long sequences of noisy scalars, which makes complex tasks hard to learn. It proposes prescriptive policy learning (PPL), which directly teaches agents high-level behavioral principles such as maintaining balance, accumulating energy, and landing smoothly, using key quantities and references to indicate at each step whether a principle is followed. Experiments show that PPL agents learn good, generalizable policies without any reward, outperform reward-based methods with far fewer samples, and transfer their policies to harder settings.

entry.title: Bayesian tensor train kernel machines that infer model complexity automatically
entry.summary: Bayesian Tensor Train Kernel Machines with Automatic Model Complexity Inference arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper proposes Bayesian Tensor Train Kernel Machines (BTT-KM) for supervised learning. Hierarchical ARD-type priors on the tensor train cores allow the TT ranks and feature dimensions to be inferred from data. Mean-field variational inference yields a Bayesian alternating least squares algorithm with the same computational complexity as its deterministic counterpart, along with a closed-form predictive distribution. A synthetic experiment shows that the method recovers the true TT ranks and feature dimensions from an over-parameterized initialization.

entry.title: Scalable Bayesian Gaussian process classification for calibrated cancer histopathology predictions under distribution shift.
entry.summary: Scalable Bayesian Gaussian Process Classification for Cancer Histopathology: Calibrated Uncertainty Under Distribution Shift arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper presents a scalable Bayesian Gaussian Process Classification framework built on frozen pathology foundation model embeddings (Phikon), combining low-rank kernel factorization, Hamiltonian Monte Carlo posterior sampling, and a pivot-based prediction scheme. It is evaluated on breast cancer metastasis detection benchmarks PCam and CAMELYON17-WILDS, the latter testing calibration under hospital-level distribution shift. The authors report improved calibration and predictive performance over stochastic variational GP and neural network baselines, with the largest gains under distribution shift.

entry.title: Tuning open-source LLM judges with soft prompts to match human annotation
entry.summary: Adapting LLM Judges to Observed Human Annotation Policy through Soft Prompt Tuning arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper studies whether soft prompt tuning can make lightweight open-source LLM judges agree more closely with human annotation policy. The authors train soft prompts on the FairBotBench benchmark and evaluate the adapted judges on bias, toxicity, and personalization. Hybrid soft-prompt tuning, which combines textual prompts with learned continuous prompt embeddings, consistently improves agreement with human annotations over untuned baselines. For Qwen 3.5 9B, the adapted judges surpass both hosted reference judges on all three dimensions.

entry.title: Data-driven modeling of molten chloride corrosion from static test data
entry.summary: Data-Driven Modeling of Molten Chloride Corrosion Using Static Test Data arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This study compiles 291 literature-reported static molten chloride corrosion experiments into a dataset and builds an interpretable machine-learning framework to predict corrosion rates. A Chloride Salt Preparation Index (CSPI) is introduced to place differences in salt preparation across studies on a common scale, and it emerges as the dominant model descriptor. A blended tree-based ensemble achieves a cross-validated R² of 0.85 and an MAE of 0.41 mg cm⁻² day⁻¹, with exposure time, temperature, and alloy chemistry also identified as important, and well-calibrated prediction intervals provided.

entry.title: Machine learning for predicting live birth after IVF/ICSI from clinical data: review and meta-analysis
entry.summary: Machine Learning for Live-Birth Prediction After IVF/ICSI From Structured Clinical Data: A Systematic Review, Meta-Analysis, and Critical Appraisal arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper systematically reviews machine-learning models that predict live birth after IVF or ICSI using routine clinical data, covering 48 included studies. Pooled discrimination was summarised with random-effects meta-analysis of the area under the ROC curve. Models evaluated only internally pooled to 0.814, versus 0.756 for those tested on later periods or other centres, with extreme heterogeneity. Most studies were at high or unclear risk of bias, no model showed evidence of clinical impact, and the certainty of evidence is low to very low.

entry.title: PromptOps: Iterative Prompt Optimization for Keeping AI Judges Accurate
entry.summary: PromptOps: Iterative Prompt Optimization for LLM-as-a-Judge Systems arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper addresses how large language models used as automated judges can drift away from intended human evaluation standards as user interactions and score distributions change. It introduces PromptOps, a closed-loop framework that monitors and iteratively recalibrates these LLM judges, separating decisions about when to optimize, which method to use, which feedback to select, and how to update the prompt. Experiments show iterative optimization can recover judge performance after controlled distribution shifts, but the best algorithm and update timing depend on context.

entry.title: Regulating Autonomous Mobility-on-Demand Operators Using Fixed and Adaptive Penalties via Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
entry.summary: Regulating Autonomous Mobility-on-Demand Operators with Fixed and Adaptive Penalties: A Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Approach arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies how penalty-based regulation can curb excessive surge pricing by autonomous mobility-on-demand operators and improve service availability across regions. Both the operator and the regulator are modeled as learning agents using graph-based multi-agent reinforcement learning. Experiments on real Manhattan data show that fixed surge pricing penalties cut the share of travelers facing excessive prices from 22% to 1%. Dynamic region-specific penalties raise the regulator's reward by up to 15.6% over fixed penalties of equal mean intensity.

entry.title: Patient-reported cancer screening barriers mined from online communities
entry.summary: What Patients Say They Can't Access: Mining Cancer Screening Barriers from Online Communities arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper analyzes over 56,000 posts from six cancer-related Reddit communities, extracting 576 posts from U.S. patients. It applies keyword filtering, barrier triage, open coding, and codebook synthesis to categorize patient-reported obstacles to cancer screening. The findings identify structural, informational, and psychosocial barriers that vary by cancer type and community context.

entry.title: Consistent yet Contextual: Learning Author-Level Style Mixtures for Authorship Attribution
entry.summary: Consistent yet Contextual: Learning Author-Level Mixtures of Style for Authorship Attribution arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper addresses authorship verification and attribution, which typically model document style rather than the authors themselves. The authors introduce several ways to model an author so that the representation captures multiple consistent but distinct writing styles, and report that this yields significant performance gains. They also study when an author's writing is most idiomatic of their style across four settings: audience size, temporal distance from training, preceding context, and genre norms.

entry.title: Server-side sparse expert assignment for federated mixture-of-experts models
entry.summary: Server-Side Sparse Assignment for Federated Mixture-of-Experts arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper proposes S³-MoE, a federated mixture-of-experts framework in which the server sparsely assigns experts to clients. It estimates each client's expert relevance from partial observations and refines assignments with an exploit-explore mechanism. The authors also give guarantees on relevance-estimation error and exact Top-K recovery. In CIFAR-100 experiments with a CNN-based MoE, each client loads only 5 experts and achieves 1.31 points higher mean final accuracy than Full-20 FedAvg, which gives every client all 20 experts.

entry.title: Large-scale symbolic models of human and machine reasoning
entry.summary: Synthesizing symbolic models of human and machine reasoning at scale arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper introduces Behavior-Conditioned Symbolic Synthesis (BCSS), a method that automatically searches for interpretable, deterministic symbolic programs that reproduce observed behavior. The authors apply BCSS to model human and machine behavior across hundreds of reasoning problems. They find that both tend to oversimplify, adopt partial explanatory rules, and misinfer dependencies between problem features. Reasoning effort predicts how much machines simplify their observations.

entry.title: Wide-View Synthesis from Multiple Cameras for Autonomous Driving
entry.summary: Wide View Synthesis from Overlapping Perspective Cameras in Autonomous Driving arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper formulates wide view synthesis (WVS), which generates a geometrically consistent wide image at a chosen virtual viewpoint from several perspective cameras. The method, Wide-View Gaussian Splatting (WV-GS), is a feed-forward Gaussian splatting framework that avoids per-scene optimization. It uses Piecewise Perspective Rendering to reduce peripheral stretching and Spatial Affine Photometric Modeling to handle photometric differences across cameras. The authors also introduce WideDrive, a synthetic benchmark, and report experiments on multiple datasets.

entry.title: When Verification Is Not Agreement: Cross-agent LLM-to-Dafny formalization
entry.summary: When Verification Is Not Agreement: Cross-Agent LLM-to-Dafny Formalization arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper studies a protocol in which one language model writes a Dafny predicate from clinical trial criteria and another writes a method checked against it. Even a same-model control agrees only 59.3% of the time when re-extracting from identical text. Across four model configurations on 96 trial documents, agreement ranges widely, and a weaker implementer can pass verification by directly invoking the specifier's predicate. The authors conclude that successful verification alone is not evidence of independent agreement.

entry.title: Automated Feedback to Peer Tutors Boosts Their Questioning and Learner Reasoning, Not Speaking Balance
entry.summary: Automated Feedback to Peer Tutors Increases Their Talk Moves and Learner Reasoning but Not the Balance of Talk arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This randomized controlled trial tested automated feedback on discourse with 1,030 volunteer tutors and 7,443 learners across two four-week SAT math bootcamps. Tutors received no feedback, feedback on their own talk, or that feedback plus participation feedback for their learners. Feedback to tutors increased eliciting of learner ideas, uptake of contributions, and learner reasoning by 8-15%. However, tutor talk time, averaging 91.5% in the control group, did not change in any condition, and learner-facing feedback added no further change.

entry.title: Finite-time convergence and regret guarantees for neural reinforcement learning in POMDPs
entry.summary: Finite-Time Convergence and Regret Guarantees for Neural Reinforcement Learning in POMDPs arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies reinforcement learning in partially observable Markov decision processes (POMDPs) by approximating them with a superstate MDP built from a truncated finite-memory history. Using nonlinear neural value function approximation, the authors prove a finite-time critic error bound for temporal-difference learning. Combined with policy mirror descent, they obtain finite-time sublinear regret against the optimal POMDP value. The authors claim this is the first such result based on neural function approximation for finite-memory POMDPs, and numerical experiments support the theory.

entry.title: Multi-agent reinforcement learning that explores cooperatively under a performance constraint
entry.summary: Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning via Epigraph-Form Guided Exploration arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper tackles cooperative exploration in multi-agent reinforcement learning, where agents must learn to coordinate in a huge joint action space. The authors propose EFXPLORER, which maximizes exploration objectives subject to a constraint that protects task performance, solved via an epigraph reformulation with adaptive exploration budgets. A successor distance-based intrinsic reward is added to encourage diverse, long-horizon exploration. Experiments on SMAX, VMAS, and MPE benchmarks report outperforming strong baselines and discovering novel cooperative strategies.

entry.title: Stochastic dynamics of generative AI, from autoregressive LLMs to interacting networks and neural SDEs
entry.summary: Stochastic Dynamics of Generative AI: From Autoregressive Models to Interacting LLM Networks and Neural SDEs arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies three types of generative AI models from a stochastic dynamical-systems perspective. It formulates large language models as high-dimensional nonlinear autoregressive models with attention-based dependencies, linking pretraining by maximum likelihood to token-by-token generation. It then analyzes networks of interacting LLMs using mean-field ordinary differential equations, covering emergent preferential attachment and persistent structural biases. Finally, it treats neural stochastic differential equations as continuous-time generative models and discusses their training via Wiener-space cubature methods based on rough-path analysis.

entry.title: Skin lesion segmentation using images generated by a text-to-image model (GENIQ)
entry.summary: Segment What It Can Draw: Querying a Text-to-Image Generator with Its Own Images for Skin Lesion Segmentation arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper presents GENIQ, a training-free method for segmenting skin lesions in dermoscopy images without annotated masks. It builds skin and lesion prototypes from images generated by a text-to-image diffusion model, then refines them using the most skin-like and lesion-like patches from unlabelled dermoscopy images. Test patches are scored along the refined direction with a gated threshold, achieving Dice scores of 0.85 to 0.88 on three test sets.

entry.title: Competitive flow matching to widen the quality-coverage frontier
entry.summary: Expanding the Quality-Coverage Frontier with Competitive Flow Matching arXiv · Nov 5, 2026Flow matching generators often trade image quality against coverage, and this paper attributes the issue to the training objective, where one noisy image can map to many clean images but the model predicts only one velocity. The authors train with a winner-take-all scheme: each example gets K candidate velocities from random low-dimensional codes, and only the best-matching candidate receives the loss. They also introduce auxiliary conditioning scaling as a new guidance mechanism alongside traditional guidance. On ImageNet-256 with SiT and RAEv2 testbeds, the method reports substantially lower FD_r,6 at matched recall points.

entry.title: Variant reclassification: spotting need for reinterpretation in online health communities
entry.summary: Reclassification Is All You Missed: Surfacing Variant Reinterpretation Need in Online Health Communities at Population Scale arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper presents PRISM, an agentic large-language-model pipeline that screens posts in online health communities, checks whether the discussed genetic variant was later reclassified, and drafts a disclaimer-bearing outreach message in a no-contact dry run. Across 3.9 million posts from 32 communities, reinterpretation-relevant discussion is rare (0.288%) but concentrated in specialist genetics communities and has grown fivefold since 2014. PRISM surfaces 123 candidate classification differences, five of which moved from uncertain to pathogenic or likely pathogenic.

entry.title: Closed-Loop Agent Evaluation: Layered Measurement and Self-Calibration
entry.summary: Closed-Loop Agent Evaluation: Layered Measurement and Self-Calibration arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper proposes a closed-loop evaluation method for deployed agents, treating evaluation as performance estimation under biased raters and censored outcomes. Conclusions at each level must trace back to atomic data and be computed by versioned rules, across span, trace, conversation and engagement levels. An inner loop audits evidence, rules and metrics, while an outer loop uses per-component regression checks to drive agent improvement. The method is applied to the business-analysis agent SharpInsight and ported to public conversation data.

entry.title: Authorization Propagation in Agent2Agent Systems: A Security Test of Multi-Hop Delegation
entry.summary: Authorization Propagation in Agent2Agent Systems: An Experimental Security Evaluation of Multi-Hop Delegation arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies security risks in delegated Agent2Agent (A2A) workflows, where the agent sending a request differs from the principal that granted the authority. The authors test a layered verification design in a synthetic four-party healthcare reimbursement workflow, rejecting 14 of 15 adversarial conditions. A separate experiment shows that a holder of the shared authorization-evidence HMAC key can alter the represented authority and produce valid evidence. The results support separating request authentication from inherited authority and call for origin-verifiable delegation and semantic attenuation.

entry.title: "Gaussians Can Subtract": Neural Dissolve Fields for Hybrid Scene Rendering
entry.summary: Gaussians Can Subtract: Neural Dissolve Fields for Hybrid Scene Rendering arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies hybrid scene rendering that combines textured meshes with 3D Gaussian primitives. The authors argue that conflicts between mesh and Gaussians are not always missing content, and can also come from geometry errors or occlusion mismatch. They propose Gaussolve, which selectively dissolves inconsistent mesh content and then refills the revealed regions with residual Gaussians. A lightweight Neural Dissolve Field learns where and from which viewing directions mesh content is dissolved, and a continuous transmittance fusion rule smoothly exposes the Gaussians. Experiments on structured and semi-structured scenes report higher visual fidelity with fewer Gaussian primitives and faster rendering.

entry.title: Adapting the Process of Adaptation: Darwinian, Lamarckian, and Agent-Directed Evolution in AI
entry.summary: Adapting the Process of Adaptation: Darwinian, Lamarckian, and Agent-Directed Evolution in AI arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper develops a theoretical framework comparing Darwinian, Lamarckian, and agent-directed evolution as ways of adapting to environmental change. It finds that agents generating and evaluating their own behavioral variants can adapt faster, but misspecified evaluation targets can drive convergence toward wrong behavior even as measured performance improves. The authors argue that independent evaluation and oversight must keep pace with autonomous AI development.

entry.title: Follow the Policy, Fail the Benchmark: Auditing and Revising Policy-Based Decision Benchmarks
