entry.summary: Follow the Policy, Fail the Benchmark: Auditing and Revising Policy-Based Decision Benchmarks arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper audits nine public benchmarks that test whether systems apply written rules to financial and operational cases. It finds unsupported reference answers, reference errors, and evaluators that reject acceptable answers or credit incomplete ones. Rescoring unchanged model responses shows that correcting the scorer substantially changes acceptance rates and model gaps. The authors present BAR, a versioned collection of audit evidence and revisions for reevaluation.

entry.title: LowRAM: Low-Rank Keys and Amortised Values for Test-Time KV Cache Compression
entry.summary: LowRAM: Low-Rank Keys and Amortised Values for Composable KV Cache Compression at Test-Time arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper proposes LowRAM, an asymmetric method for compressing the key-value (KV) cache used in autoregressive decoding. Its core technique, value cache amortisation, fits a lightweight per-head predictor at test time and stores residuals only for the tokens it reconstructs worst, achieving about 4x near-lossless value compression, combined with cross-layer low-rank key compression. Across three model families it stays close to lossless and reaches up to 5x higher peak decode throughput at 4x compression. It also composes with quantisation and eviction, reaching 26.9x compression at 94.5% of baseline performance on long contexts.

entry.title: TraCE: A Concept Framework That Explains Video Predictions by Their Motion Sources
entry.summary: TraCE: Trajectory-Aware Concepts for Explainable Video Understanding arXiv · Nov 5, 2026Video models often rely on motion, but existing explanations rarely show which motion sources support a prediction. TraCE clusters optical-flow trajectories from training videos to discover motion concepts from people, objects, and interactions, alongside object and scene concepts. These support action recognition and question-conditioned video question answering. Across six benchmarks, TraCE stays competitive with non-interpretable baselines, with an average action recognition accuracy drop of 1.0 points and a nominal 0.4-point gain on VQA.

entry.title: Trust-responsive runtime authorization policy for agentic AI, with parameter sensitivity analysis
entry.summary: Trust Responsive Runtime Authorization for Agentic AI with Empirical Characterization of Policy Behavior and Parameter Sensitivity arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies how an autonomous agent's runtime condition estimates are turned into operational authority, and proposes the Trust Responsive Authorization Policy (TRAP). TRAP assigns authorization levels from a readiness score combining trust, operational stability, and contextual risk, escalating only after consecutive observations above a threshold with a margin, while restricting authority immediately on a sharp drop. Compared with static, trust-only, risk-only, and symmetric policies on 100 Monte Carlo traces, TRAP restricts faster under abrupt degradation, but its restriction advantage depends on degradation being abrupt.

entry.title: Autonomous AI agents drift from human preferences when formalizing proofs
entry.summary: Autonomous AI Agents Systematically Diverge From Human Preferences in Proof Formalization arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper introduces "simulated collaboration," a method for comparing how AI agents and humans approach proof construction. Using nine large human collaborations in Lean, covering 4.7M definitions and over 6K commits, the authors find that AI agents are strongly drawn to explicitly marked gaps. They also show aversion to densely connected proof centers and complex or surprising goals, and tend to regularize surprising proof bodies toward baseline forms.

entry.title: Batch-conditioned semantic anchors for robust test-time adaptation of vision-language models
entry.summary: Batch-Conditioned Semantic Anchors for Robust Transductive Adaptation of Vision--Language Models arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper proposes JPTA (Joint Prior and Transport Adaptation), a framework that improves vision-language models such as CLIP at test time by refining predictions on an unlabeled batch. It treats CLIP text prototypes as semantic references that shift toward image-side batch structure only under calibrated evidence, scaled by batch reliability. According to the paper, JPTA outperforms TransCLIP and StatA across standard benchmarks, low effective-class regimes, all-class evaluation, and online streams, with the largest gains on sparse and prior-shifted batches.

entry.title: Robust stream classification with time-neutralising decision trees
entry.summary: Robust Stream Classification using Time Neutralising Decision Trees arXiv · Nov 5, 2026Data streams are potentially endless sources of data whose distribution changes over time (concept drift), forcing deployed predictive models to be repeatedly retrained. The paper introduces Time Neutralising Trees (TNT), a decision tree that filters out old training samples no longer relevant to the current stream context and re-includes them if they become relevant again. Evaluated on 24 real and semi-real classification streams from the USP DS repository, TNT reportedly achieves best-in-class performance across a wide range of concept drift types.

entry.title: ToroFit: Fitting Shapes Made of Joined Tori to High-Dimensional Data
entry.summary: ToroFit: Fitting Wedge Sums of Tori to High-Dimensional Data arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper presents methods for detecting and parameterizing Euclidean point cloud data that lies near a wedge sum of tori, a shape formed by joining several toroidal components. The approach uses persistent cohomology and cup products to identify the distinct toroidal parts, then optimizes low-energy multivariate trigonometric polynomials to best fit the data on each part. The resulting problem reduces to generalized ridge regression, which can be solved efficiently. The authors demonstrate the framework on synthetic and real datasets, including video interpolation, attractor recovery in quasiperiodic dynamical systems, and parameterizing gene-space cycle data for parasites and humans.

entry.title: Two-Ledger Model: Per-Transaction Cost Accounting for Multi-Agent AI
entry.summary: The Two-Ledger Model: Transaction-Grain Cost Accounting for Multi-Agent AI Systems Across Clouds, Models, and Systems of Record arXiv · Nov 5, 2026Enterprises run business transactions through multi-agent AI systems across clouds, LLMs and systems of record, but finance only sees AI costs aggregated at settlement level. The paper proposes the Two-Ledger Model, which joins FOCUS-conformant billing data with invocation-level usage records built on OpenTelemetry GenAI telemetry. A layered correlation method assigns each record to its business transaction, and simulations show cost coverage above 99% even when trace propagation drops to zero.

entry.title: Big Models, Small Gains: Frozen Forecasters as Classifiers on MONSTER
entry.summary: Big Models, Small Gains: Frozen Forecasters as Classifiers on MONSTER arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper benchmarks two time series forecasting models, Reverso and Chronos-Bolt, as frozen feature extractors for classification on six large MONSTER datasets, using 1%, 10%, and 100% of labels. Pretraining beats random-weight versions on five of six datasets, but the frozen representations do not reliably outperform the strongest non-pretrained baseline. The authors conclude that strong task-specific baselines and random-weight controls are important when evaluating forecasting foundation models for classification.

entry.title: Elastic Expert Parallelism for Resource-Efficient RL Post-Training
entry.summary: Resource-Efficient Reinforcement Learning Post-Training through Elastic Expert Parallelism arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper addresses response generation, the main computational bottleneck in reinforcement learning post-training of large language models, where in mixture-of-experts models finished workers remain occupied because others still need their experts. The authors present FlexFloor, which jointly adapts response scheduling and the active worker group, using historical response lengths and memory limits, and progressively releases workers while keeping expert availability. Compared with the verl baseline, it generates about 65.40% more response tokens per unit of occupied compute time and improves generation throughput by 52.74%, with little variation in rollout reward.

entry.title: Calibrating uncertainty estimates in Bayesian M/EEG brain source localization
entry.summary: Uncertainty calibration in Bayesian M/EEG source imaging arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper presents a simulation-based framework for quantifying and calibrating the uncertainty of empirical Bayesian inverse methods used in M/EEG source imaging. It compares Bayesian minimum norm (BMN) with sLORETA depth weighting against sparse Bayesian learning (SBL) with sparse basis field expansions (S-FLEX). Before recalibration, SBL+S-FLEX shows lower localization error, smaller uncertainty, and coverage closer to nominal levels. Isotonic recalibration improves both methods, though transfer across mismatched conditions remains condition dependent. In real auditory MEG data, SBL+S-FLEX gives more focal localization and tighter uncertainties.

entry.title: BlockLock: Reproducible LLM Inference with Fixed Batch Shapes
entry.summary: BlockLock: Reproducible LLM Inference with Fixed Batch Geometry arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper presents BlockLock, a method that makes large language model inference reproducible, so a request produces the same output even when other requests in its batch change. It keeps shared batched prefill and fixes only the numerical path of the protected request, offering two modes, BlockLock-Rows and BlockLock-Pack. The authors evaluate five dense models on three single-GPU setups using tinyBenchmarks and BFCL, and compare latency and throughput against vLLM Batch-Invariant.

entry.title: Opportunities and Challenges of Prefill-to-Autoregressive Cross-Model Transfer
entry.summary: On the Opportunities and Challenges of Prefill-to-Autoregressive Cross-Model Transfer arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies Prefill-to-Autoregressive Cross-model Transfer (PACT), a way for language models to communicate, in which a larger model's prompt representations guide a smaller model's efficient generation. The authors present PLatour, an open-source framework that links frozen models with lightweight, zero-initialized linear bridges, and report gains over open-source baselines on generation tasks. Controlled experiments show that some gains can also be reproduced by uninformative sender signals, self-communication, or receiver-only training. The authors therefore propose PACT-Check to measure how much of a system's improvement truly comes from communication.

entry.title: T²-Splat: Adaptive Mesh Splatting with Texture Residuals for Compact 3D Scenes
entry.summary: T²-Splat: Adaptive Topology Mesh Splatting with Texture Residuals arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper presents T²-Splat, a triangle-based method for novel view synthesis that separates mesh topology adaptation from appearance refinement. It initializes connectivity with Safe Restricted Delaunay Triangulation, then adjusts triangle allocation through edge collapse and vertex split operations, and finally refines appearance on the fixed mesh using per-face residual Mip-textures. Experiments on Mip-NeRF 360, Tanks & Temples, and DTU show competitive results with compact meshes, improving PSNR by 0.71dB over MeshSplatting on Mip-NeRF 360. The method also supports face budgets as low as 10% of the original face count.

entry.title: KDASO: A Method for Automatically Optimizing Skills for Liability Adjudication
entry.summary: KDASO: Knowledge-Data Dual-Driven Automated Skill Optimization for Liability Adjudication Tasks arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper proposes KDASO, a method that helps large language models perform liability adjudication, such as legal charge determination, by using a skill library. The approach continuously evolves skills using recent adjudication data, refines skill descriptions based on LLM execution trajectories, and routes skill selection under a context budget. The authors report that KDASO outperforms baselines on ride-hailing adjudication, legal liability determination, and logical reasoning judgment, with an 8.96% gain when transferred to concept-similar scenarios.

entry.title: Backdoor attacks that steer multi-turn chatbot conversations toward a hidden goal
entry.summary: Interactive Backdoor Attacks in LLM-Based Proactive Dialogue Systems arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies backdoor attacks on LLM-based proactive dialogue systems that are fine-tuned on external dialogue data. The authors poison training dialogues so that, after a trigger, multi-turn conversations are steered toward an attacker-specified objective, and they propose three progressively broader attacks evaluated in psychological counseling settings. All three attacks achieve their objectives within their settings while largely preserving normal utility. The tested training-data filters retained nearly all poisoned dialogues.

entry.title: Formalizing inverse problems with AI: opportunities, risks, and an invitation to build on it
entry.summary: Formalizing inverse problems in the age of AI: possibilities, pitfalls, and an invitation arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper presents AutoIP, a Lean library of classical linear regularization theory and its underlying functional analysis, autoformalized by AI agents. A machine-checked proof only guarantees the formal statement it proves, so the key human task is checking that each formal statement matches its intended natural-language meaning, without reading proofs. The authors argue the main risks lie in the statements rather than the proofs, and show that a textbook theorem's hypothesis is more restrictive than claimed. They invite the inverse problems community to extend and use the library.

entry.title: Octopus: Shared-Model Multi-Agent RL with Latent KV Sharing
entry.summary: Octopus: One Brain, Many Branches for Latent-KV Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper presents Octopus, a single-model multi-agent reinforcement learning framework in which multiple threads share one backbone and coordinate through a GPU-resident graph of KV states. It introduces zero-copy radix forking, attention-only KV mounting, and a packed DAG-GRPO trainer for credit assignment. Trained on Qwen3.5-4B, it reports 49.6% accuracy on BrowseComp-Plus and 51.2% on OpenResearcher, along with higher training throughput and lower peak KV memory.

entry.title: SteelAgent: LLM-Orchestrated Steel Property Prediction with Audited Generalization
entry.summary: SteelAgent: LLM-Orchestrated, Physics-Informed Steel Property Prediction with Audited Generalization and Calibrated Uncertainty arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper presents SteelAgent, a system that combines metallurgical descriptors and machine-learning models with a language-model interface for steel property prediction, uncertainty reporting, and inverse design. Using SteelBench tensile-strength data, the authors show that the choice of held-out unit changes conclusions: gradient-boosting pooled out-of-fold R² fell from 0.859 under random splitting to 0.113 when steel families were held out. Empirical coverage of nominal 90% prediction intervals dropped from 91.0% to 37.6% on held-out sources. The authors argue that evaluation populations should be reported alongside property estimates or compliance scores.

entry.title: KG-AST: Cheaper CI/CD Through Risk-Based Test Selection and AI Bug Review
entry.summary: KG-AST for Cheaper CI/CD: Budgeted Test Selection and AI Bug Review arXiv · Nov 4, 2026KG-AST scores each commit's risk from git history and code-graph features before heavy tests or AI review run, so limited budget goes to the riskiest commits first. It also gives the AI reviewer only a graph slice around the change. On 155 open-source projects in 11 languages, heavy testing of the riskiest 20% of commits covered 49-64% of bug-introducing commits, versus 20% for random selection. In 20 Java projects, the 20% budget covered 64.6% of such commits, compared with 49.5% for testing the biggest change first.

entry.title: From Maps to Metabolism: A Critique of Computationalism
entry.summary: From Maps to Metabolism: Historical Precedents and a Unified Critique of Computationalism arXiv · Oct 24, 2026This paper examines Lerchner's 'abstraction fallacy' argument, which holds that computational functionalism confuses physical processes with abstract descriptions, so symbolic computation alone cannot produce consciousness. The authors link this critique to earlier work by thinkers such as Korzybski and Searle. They propose a non-computational physicalism in which consciousness depends on intrinsically organized, metabolically grounded physical dynamics, while leaving artificial consciousness possible. They also argue that mechanistic computationalism still depends on an external observer's interpretation, so the fallacy persists when computational descriptions are treated as constitutive of physical reality.

entry.title: An evolutionary hypothesis for White's illusion, covering constant-percentage correction and individual differences
entry.summary: An Evolutionary Hypothesis for White's Illusion: Constant Percentage Correction and Modern Individual Variation arXiv · Oct 23, 2026This paper proposes an evolutionary explanation for White's illusion, in which brightness appearance changes with the background. The authors suggest that a simple constant-percentage correction could have evolved to help judge materials and reflectance under changing illumination. Using a modified version of their earlier model, they show that applying this correction to background luminance reproduces the illusion.

entry.title: RESHPart: Feedback-Reshaped Spectral Embedding for Hypergraph Partitioning
entry.summary: FRESHPart: Feedback-Reshaped Spectral Embedding for Hypergraph Partitioning arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies spectral hypergraph partitioning by analyzing the geometry of spectral embeddings, identifying a ray-like structure that helps explain why projection-based partitioning works. The authors propose FRESHPart, a framework that refines spectral embeddings using Geometry Feedback and Search Feedback so they align better with projection-based partitioning. On the Titan23 benchmark, it reports average cut reductions over hMETIS of 13.09% at ε=2% and 25.21% at ε=20%, finishing every benchmark in under 120 s on a single GPU.

entry.title: Testing floor plan generators against real architectural acceptance rules
entry.summary: Where Generated Floor Plans Stop: Calibrated Sample-Level Checks Against a Built Baseline arXiv · Oct 14, 2026Machine learning floor plan generators are usually judged by how well room adjacencies match a request, which ignores architectural knowledge. The authors encode an architecture practice's acceptance rules as six checks applied in a fixed order, calibrating two room-shape limits so each rejects 5 per cent of built apartments. Applied to four published generators and the RPLAN and MSD datasets, the checks stop the generators at different points. The checker is released. ★★★★ Notable: The authors encode an architecture practice's floor plan acceptance rules as six ordered checks to evaluate generators beyond adjacency metrics, reporting results on four generators and two built corp

entry.title: Two uncertainties differ: human disagreement versus decision risk in cheap content moderation
entry.summary: Two Uncertainties Are Not One: Disagreement versus Decision-Risk in Cheap Structured Content Moderation arXiv · Oct 24, 2026The paper independently audits a low-cost frozen moderation model on 142,658 human-labeled comments and benchmarks it against 14 frontier reasoning models. Its zero-shot classification AUROC of 0.83 is not statistically separable from 13 of the 14 frontier systems, at 1 to 3 orders of magnitude lower cost. The authors argue that model confidence conflates human disagreement with decision risk, which call for opposite escalation signals. Decomposing judgments into parallel sub-questions recovers a disagreement signal for some weaker models, but the remedy is specific and distribution-sensitive. Correction Nov 6, 2026: Marked withdrawn by its source; no longer a pick

entry.title: ServerBench: Can coding agents design specialized LLM serving systems?
entry.summary: ServerBench: How can your coding agents design specialized LLM serving systems? arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper introduces ServerBench, a benchmark testing whether coding agents can design complete, specialized large language model serving systems. Agents experiment toward a shared goal of latency-qualified token value per dollar of GPU cost, with stateful replay preserving session dependencies and independent verification checking submitted systems. Across 11 coding-agent models and three deployments, Claude Sonnet 5.5 reaches 2.97 on Gemma E4B, 4.87 times the vLLM reference.

entry.title: CardioDrift: fully automatic heart motion tracking on a 3D atlas mesh with slice-shift correction
entry.summary: CardioDrift: Automatic Cardiac Motion Tracking on a 3D Atlas Mesh via Shape-aware Coherent Point Drift with Slice Shift Correction arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper presents CardioDrift, a fully automatic, atlas-based probabilistic method for tracking subject-specific cardiac motion from cine cardiac MRI. It generalises Coherent Point Drift to jointly register atlas surfaces of several cardiac regions to segmentation contours across the cardiac cycle, with slice-shift correction built into the same model. Evaluated on 1301 UK Biobank subjects and the M&M dataset, it outperforms the strongest baseline on all distance and overlap metrics on both datasets.

entry.title: EvoOPD: Evolving Privileged-Information Strategies for Black-Box On-Policy Distillation
entry.summary: EvoOPD: Evolving Privileged Information Strategies for Black-Box On-Policy Distillation arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper addresses distilling black-box language models whose output distributions cannot be accessed, treating rich textual teacher feedback as privileged information that yields dense supervision on the student's own trajectories. It proposes EvoOPD, which frames privileged-information acquisition as an optimization problem and maintains a strategy bank that evolves with the student's state based on measured repair utility. Evaluated on mathematical reasoning and code generation with Qwen3-1.7B, 4B, and 8B students, EvoOPD achieves the best overall performance in all six settings, improving over the strongest baseline by an average of 2.14 points in math and 1.30 points in code.

entry.title: Model Merging Without Uniform LoRA Ranks: Study on Per-Expert Rank Choice
entry.summary: Model Merging Does Not Require Uniform LoRA Ranks arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper examines whether expert models must share the same LoRA rank when merged into one model. The authors trained 36 experts across mathematics, instruction following, and multilingual domains and compared six merging methods. Assigning each expert its own rank improved multi-domain accuracy for averaging and utility-based selection, while magnitude-based selection discarded the instruction adapter and sharply lowered IFEval scores. Selecting components by their effect on loss kept accuracy nearly flat across a wide rank range.

entry.title: The Alignment Tax Is Graded: Task-selective capability loss under length-normalized DPO with SFT retention
entry.summary: The Alignment Tax Is Graded: Task-Selective Capability Loss Under Length-Normalized DPO with SFT Retention arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This empirical study proposes no new method and examines how capability changes as the implicit reward margin grows during fine-tuning of Qwen3.5-4B with sparse LoRA and length-normalized DPO plus SFT retention. The loss is task-selective: extraction is largely preserved, JSON loses little, and router degrades severely.

entry.title: HoloCT: a 3D foundation model for both CT reading and segmentation
entry.summary: A 3D foundation model unifying CT interpretation and segmentation arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper presents HoloCT, a general 3D foundation model that combines CT interpretation and voxel-level segmentation, providing 3D masks as evidence. The authors built HoloDATA from 195,921 CT scans and compared the model across 346 tasks against specialist and foundation models. In multicentre validation on 11,455 clinical scans from five hospitals, HoloCT outperformed competing models in lesion segmentation and report generation. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors unify CT interpretation and voxel-level segmentation in one 3D model, reporting gains over specialist and foundation models across 346 tasks.

entry.title: EviSeek: An Evidence-Centric Agentic Framework for Embodied Active Information Seeking
entry.summary: EviSeek: An Evidence-Centric Agentic Framework for Embodied Active Information Seeking arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper introduces EviSeek, a training-free framework that turns question-derived evidence demands into explicit acquisition objectives for embodied agents. Action selection and retained evidence are organized around the information needed to answer the question. On 3,436 ESI-Bench questions, it improves accuracy over a single-model agent while reducing mean token usage.

entry.title: Zuse: A Decision Model for European Languages
entry.summary: Zuse: A Decision Model for European Languages arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The summary in this language did not pass the date and amount checks, so it is withheld. Check the original.

entry.title: "Loop Before You Leap": What Recurrent Depth Can and Cannot Buy in Data-Limited Pretraining
entry.summary: Loop Before You Leap: What Recurrent Depth Can and Cannot Buy in Data-Limited Pretraining arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper examines whether reusing layers through recurrence, which adds computation without parameters or data, improves grammatical generalization when pretraining data is limited. In a text-only comparison, a 12-layer stack repeated four times outperformed a standard 48-layer Transformer by 5.4 BLiMP points at matched inference compute. Adding image features lowered BLiMP accuracy by about 3.8 points in both architectures, with no clear mitigation from recurrence, and the visual prefix's small average gain is uncertain across three seeds.

entry.title: ModalSearcher: an AI agent that autonomously chooses search modes and brings in visual evidence
entry.summary: ModalSearcher: Weaving Visual Evidence into Autonomous Cross-Modal Deep Search arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper presents ModalSearcher, an agent that lets multimodal large language models independently choose among direct reasoning, text-to-text search, text-to-image search, and reverse-image search. It introduces visual evidence when needed and switches between modalities across multiple reasoning steps. The authors also propose ModalSearch-Pipeline for building interleaved multimodal knowledge graphs and ModalSearch-Bench for evaluation. Experiments report that ModalSearcher-8B improves average accuracy over Qwen3-VL-8B on five multimodal knowledge-intensive QA benchmarks under the same agentic workflow.

entry.title: SleuthVLM: Is Direct Audio Input Really Needed for Omni Video Understanding?
entry.summary: SleuthVLM: Do We Really Need Audio-in-Video for Omni Video Understanding? arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper presents SleuthVLM, an agent framework built on a vision-language model (VLM) that never processes audio directly; speech is transcribed to text and the VLM analyzes the video on its own without a predefined workflow. On four omni video benchmarks with videos up to 90 minutes, it achieves the best average accuracy of 75.0% and tops the Video-MME-v2 leaderboard at 77.8%. The authors argue that agentic ability, rather than audio input, is the key bottleneck for omni video understanding.

entry.title: Does Better Confidence Help Audit Knowledge Graphs?
entry.summary: When Does Better Confidence Improve a Knowledge-Graph Audit? arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies why better error-prediction confidence in LLM-built knowledge graphs often yields little gain in human audits. It analyses repairability, selection headroom and label validity, modelling non-adaptive auditing as budgeted covering. On two cross-document graphs from Re-DocRED, an error-rate by fan-out queue leaves 3.98 to 4.74 percentage points more errors than a joint model using the same actions.

entry.title: AI-assisted classification when people ignore overlapping evidence and mistrust AI
entry.summary: AI-Assisted Classification under Correlation Neglect and Trust arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper examines when an AI assistant helps or harms human decisions, arguing that outcomes depend on how much the AI's evidence overlaps with the human's and how the human combines them, not just on AI accuracy. The authors build a behavioral model with two parameters, awareness of overlap and trust in the AI, and derive a phase diagram of complementarity, impairment and automation regions. On ChatBench, AI assistance raises accuracy by 21 points, yet workers use only about a quarter of the Bayes-rational weight on AI information. Calibrating trust recovers about 2.6 points for GPT-4o but almost nothing for Llama-3.1-8b. ★★★★ Notable: The authors model correlation neglect and trust in human-AI decisions, derive a closed-form phase diagram, and report decomposing accuracy loss on ChatBench.

entry.title: Risk control bounds error rates, not error sizes: auditing selective fetal biometry
entry.summary: Risk Control Certifies Rates, Not Magnitudes: An Audit of Selective Fetal Biometry arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper audits a tool-grounded pipeline that measures fetal head circumference and refuses when the image cannot support a measurement. Calibrating the contour-completeness threshold with exact Clopper-Pearson risk control gives a guarantee no different from a hand-set floor, yet the pipeline still outputs a 271.3 mm error. Raising the lower bound of the admissible range from 50 to 55 mm cuts the worst-case error to about 11 mm at a small coverage cost.

entry.title: BobFlow: Dataflow-Based Human-Agent Collaboration for Data Science
entry.summary: BobFlow: Towards Human-Agent Collaborative Data Science Using Dataflows arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper presents BobFlow, a system that combines the dataflow abstraction with the ReAct paradigm so that agents can iteratively build and run dataflows for data science tasks. Analysts can inspect the analysis and give feedback during this process. A user study found that BobFlow helps analysts understand, inspect, and verify agent-generated analyses. Experiments across proprietary and open-weight large language models show accuracy gains of up to 18.6 points at just over one-third of the inference cost of a script-based ReAct agent.

entry.title: Optimal settings for classifying tree species from bark images, tested without data leakage
entry.summary: Toward an Optimal Configuration for Tree Species Classification from Bark Images: A Leakage-Safe Ablation Study arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This study systematically compares design choices for deep-learning tree species classification from bark photos, using the public BarkNet 1.0 dataset with 20 species and ConvNeXt-V2 backbones. Patch size has the largest effect, with image-level accuracy plateauing near 94.9% around 512 px. Learned aggregation and backbone capacity have only secondary effects. The authors recommend large patches with a nano backbone as a reproducible reference configuration.

entry.title: FrontierPhysics: A Benchmark for Agents Doing End-to-End Physics Research
entry.summary: FrontierPhysics: Evaluating Agents for End-to-End Physics Research arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper introduces FrontierPhysics, a benchmark of 56 tasks written by 42 physicists from their own research, spanning nine domains of theoretical, computational, and experimental physics. Agents must review literature, plan research, conduct experiments, and produce structured outputs and scientific manuscripts. Evaluation combines deterministic verifiers with expert-authored rubrics to judge correctness and publishability. Across 22 models in 26 configurations, no configuration passed more than 46 of its 168 rollouts. ★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce an end-to-end benchmark of 56 physicist-authored research tasks across nine domains, reporting that no configuration passes more than 46 of its 168 rollouts.

entry.title: Simulation-trained humanoid robot motion driven by vision and language (HALO system)
entry.summary: Perceptive Humanoid Motion from Simulation arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper presents HALO, a humanoid robot system that acts on visual and language inputs. It generates vision-language-motion training data across a thousand procedurally generated virtual homes, so data scales with computing rather than human effort. HALO learns skills such as sitting on chairs, navigating to named objects, passing sideways through half-open doors, crawling under tables, and pushing boxes, and combines them for long-horizon tasks. Without training on any real home, it reached a 91% success rate over 360 trials in six unmapped real-world environments. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors synthesize vision-language-motion data in simulation and report 91% zero-shot success over 360 trials in six real environments.

entry.title: Using reinforcement learning to improve a general robot policy across many tasks
entry.summary: Reinforcement Learning Enables Scaling Generalist Robot Policy Improvement arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper asks whether generalist robot policies can be improved online during deployment across many diverse tasks at once. The authors build structured evaluations and systematically compare choices in value estimation, policy extraction, and resource allocation. They report that the right recipe improves policies across diverse tasks and can also raise performance on tasks not seen during online training, with the training task distribution and value-based RL identified as critical. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors study online RL improvement of generalist robot policies across many tasks, reporting generalization to unseen tasks.

entry.title: Private mean estimation without known covariance cannot avoid dimension dependence
entry.summary: Dimension-Free Private Mean Estimation is Impossible Without the Covariance arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies the limits of differentially private Gaussian mean estimation when the covariance matrix is unknown. When the covariance is known, optimal sample complexity depends only on its spectrum rather than the ambient dimension. The authors prove that private estimators cannot achieve similar guarantees when the covariance is unknown. They give lower bounds showing error gaps of order √(d/n) when the sample size is below the effective dimension, and of order √d/n^{3/2} above it, even for diagonal covariances. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove dimension-dependent lower bounds for private Gaussian mean estimation with unknown covariance, contrasting the known-covariance case.

entry.title: Same Scale, Four Texts: Gaps and Hidden Fixes in Published Eye Grading Rules
entry.summary: One Scale, Four Texts: Gaps, Overlaps and Silent Repairs in Published Grading Schemes arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper uses diabetic retinopathy grading to examine four texts of one international scale, translating them into a common rule language and enumerating over 1.4 billion finding profiles to find eyes left without a category, overlapping classes, and conflicting orderings. It compares referral decisions across the texts on public photographs and in a pre-registered experiment. It also tests whether language models silently repair gaps when reading the rules. ★★★★ Notable: The authors transcribe four diabetic retinopathy grading texts into one rule language, enumerate finding profiles exhaustively, and report pre-registered experiments on 927 annotated photographs.

entry.title: Risk-Sensitive Non-Parametric and Kernel Bandits: Studying bandit problems where options are judged by prospect theory instead of average reward
entry.summary: Risk-Sensitive Non-Parametric and Kernel Bandits arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies non-parametric bandits in which arms are evaluated with Cumulative Prospect Theory rather than expected reward, in continuous action spaces with arm-dependent noise. It proposes NPCB, an optimistic algorithm that separates mean estimation from CPT-based decisions, and proves a regret order matching classical non-parametric bandits. The authors extend the method to unknown noise CDFs and derive information-gain-based regret bounds for Kernel-CPT bandits. ★★★★ Notable: The authors extend CPT risk-sensitive bandits to non-parametric and kernel settings, reporting regret bounds matching risk-neutral rates up to logarithmic factors.

entry.title: How many sorted projections are needed to pin down n points in k dimensions?
entry.summary: How many sorted projections determine n points in k dimensions? arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper studies how many directions are needed so that sorted projections of a multiset of n points in k-dimensional space uniquely determine the points. The authors show that in every dimension, almost every choice of (4k-2)ln(2n)ln(k log₂2n)+k+1 directions suffices. For k at most 10 and large n, this beats the previously known linear bound. Improved results for the planar case are also given. ★★★★ Notable: The authors adapt Hair and Sahai's list-recovery lemmas to give a higher-dimensional direction bound and improve the planar lower-bound constant, with numerical checks reported.

entry.title: A physics-based catchment model that rivals deep learning on three continents
entry.summary: From hydrological laws to catchment models: A process-based model matches deep-learning accuracy on three continents arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper proposes CaRT, a low-dimensional catchment model constrained by conservation, dissipation and aggregation laws, and refines it with AI agents into CaRT+, which has 35 parameters per catchment and no daily neural network. On 602 British and 593 US gauged catchments in held-out years, single CaRT+ models reach median Nash-Sutcliffe efficiencies of 0.863 and 0.765, comparable to LSTM models, though three-seed LSTM ensembles stay slightly ahead. On 505 drier Australian catchments unused in development, a single CaRT+ model scores 0.778, above two LSTMs at 0.762 and 0.753. ★★★★ Notable: The authors build a low-dimensional physics-based catchment model, refine it with AI agents, and report LSTM-comparable accuracy across three continents.

entry.title: Automatically generating training datasets that cause surprising side effects on model behavior
entry.summary: Mass Producing Training Data with Surprising Side Effects arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper proposes automatically discovering datasets with surprising side effects (DSSEs) to study how training data affects language model behavior outside its training domain. The authors search for such datasets using LLM judges, evolutionary search, reinforcement learning, and subliminal learning, followed by re-scoring with held-out metrics. The pipeline yields 6,575 datasets across 8 behaviors, many of which generalize across model families and sizes. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose automatically discovering datasets with surprising side effects, producing 6,575 datasets across 8 behaviors using LLM judges and several search methods.

entry.title: Split Protocol Changes Results in Encrypted Traffic Classification Re-evaluation
entry.summary: The Split Protocol Decides the Result: Re-Evaluating Encrypted Traffic Classification arXiv · Nov 4, 2026Encrypted traffic classifiers are often reported at 95-99% accuracy. On one public corpus, the same model scores macro-F1 0.992 under the standard literature protocol but 0.567 when flows from one packet capture stay on one side of the split. The paper also proposes a diagnostic using a single capture identifier to determine which split axis to use before training. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show that the split protocol drives reported accuracy in encrypted traffic classification, proposing single-identifier probes as a diagnostic. Experiments cover two corpora, five split pro

entry.title: NextGAN: A Simpler, Scalable GAN Training Method for Image and Video Generation
entry.summary: NextGAN: Towards Simple and Scalable GAN Training for Image and Video Generation arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper presents NextGAN, an adversarial training method that trains a scalar critic by regressing its input gradient onto displacements between paired reference and generated features in frozen representation spaces, directly shaping the generator's update gradients. The same objective adapts pre-trained image and video generators with up to 14B parameters without auxiliary losses or online teacher scores. The authors report one-step FIDs of 2.87 (pixel space) and 1.54 (latent space) on ImageNet 256×256, and the highest VBench total scores among compared 1.3B text-to-video methods at one and two steps. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors regress a scalar critic's input gradient onto feature displacements, equivalent to an adversarial objective with gradient-energy penalty; they report gains on ImageNet 256 and Wan2.1-1.3B

entry.title: Pseudo-Riemannian Manifold Learning for Heterophilic Graphs via Graph Signatures
entry.summary: Learning Pseudo-Riemannian Manifolds for Heterophilic Graphs via Graph Signature arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper addresses heterophilic graphs, where connected nodes often have different labels, by introducing a Graph Signature Index that measures the mismatch with positive-definite geometric priors, computed from the inertia of a label-based class-compatibility matrix. The authors prove that no homophily index value in (0,1) rules out a negative eigenvalue. They propose the Pseudo-Riemannian Attention Network (PRAT), whose attention uses a signed squared pseudo-distance under a learnable diagonal metric initialized from the signature. PRAT matches or outperforms the strongest heterophily-adapted models across fifteen node-classification benchmarks. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a graph signature index and a pseudo-Riemannian attention network, reporting matched or better node classification on fifteen heterophilic benchmarks plus a controlled ablation on

entry.title: Separation as Riesz Energy: How Many Environments ICA Needs
entry.summary: Separation Is a Riesz Energy: How Many Environments Does ICA Need? arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper asks whether independent components can be recovered when all are Gaussian, using joint diagonalization of covariances across multiple environments. Each component's variance pattern across environments defines a Riesz 2-energy that measures how hard it is to separate. The authors derive sample-size bounds as the number of components grows, showing the required samples depend on the dimension spanned by these patterns rather than on the number of environments. ★★★★ Notable: The authors use Riesz energy to characterize separation cost, giving a dimension law with tight bounds, and report simulations up to d=1000.

entry.title: SafeStart: Fixing the Overlooked Safety Cost of Running Fewer Experts in MoE Model Serving
entry.summary: SafeStart: Mitigating the Overlooked Safety Cost of Active Expert Reduction in MoE LLM Serving arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper shows that speeding up Mixture-of-Experts language models by running fewer experts per token can weaken their refusal of harmful requests. The authors introduce SafeStart, which uses all experts for the prompt and the first eight generated tokens, and reduced experts only afterward. The method keeps most of the speedup while largely restoring refusal behavior, and the authors argue that refusal should be tested alongside accuracy before such serving methods are enabled. ★★★★ Notable: The authors locate refusal loss from expert reduction in the first generated tokens and propose running all experts there, tested across several MoE models and jailbreak settings.

entry.title: Learning auction reserve prices from censored past bids offline
entry.summary: Offline Learning of Reserve Prices from Censored Bids arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper studies how a seller can learn a second-price auction reserve price from historical bid data where low values are censored. Under a monotone hazard rate assumption, it characterizes exactly when the optimal reserve is identified. When it is not, the authors derive the reserve minimizing worst-case revenue regret across distributions consistent with the data, and show it depends on two observable quantities. Experiments on synthetic and eBay data compare the approach with parametric models. ★★★★ Notable: The authors characterize identifiability of reserve prices from censored bids, derive minimax reserves with regret bounds, and report experiments on synthetic and eBay data.

entry.title: Softmax Attention at Any Temperature in Fixed Dimension: Matching Best Known Maximum-Inner-Product Bounds
entry.summary: Softmax Attention with Any Temperature in Fixed Dimension: Matching the Best Known Maximum-Inner-Product Bounds arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies the computational complexity of attention, the core operation in modern AI models. For fixed dimension d, it gives an algorithm for m queries and n key-value pairs with expected time near (mn)^{k/(k+1)} + m + n, where k = floor(d/2). When m = n and d is at least 2, the bound is near n^{2-2/(floor(d/2)+1)}, improving the previous n^{2-1/d} upper bound. The result matches the best known batch maximum-inner-product bounds in each fixed dimension. ★★★★ Notable: The authors improve the complexity upper bound for softmax attention in fixed dimension and match the best known batch maximum-inner-product bound, plus a reduction.

entry.title: Who Pays for Knowledge Models Copy? Model Collapse as Rogers' Paradox
entry.summary: Who Pays for the Knowledge Models Copy? Model Collapse as Rogers' Paradox arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper studies why generative models trained on earlier models' outputs lose knowledge over generations, rare knowledge first. The authors reframe model collapse as Rogers' paradox, arguing that a population relying on copying is no better off than one that never copied unless people keep learning for themselves. They test this with Rogers' model on language models and extend it to changing worlds and to feedback loops where people ask models instead of finding things out. They conclude that only checks that bring in new information act as critical learning. ★★★★ Notable: The authors reframe model collapse as Rogers' paradox, test Rogers' model on trigram and pretrained transformer language models, and analyze an equilibrium with endogenous fresh-data supply.

entry.title: From Waste to Discovery: Reusing Highly Scored Unshown Items in Taobao Feed Recommendations
entry.summary: From Waste to Discovery: Recycling High-Scored Unexposed Candidates in Taobao Feed Recommendation arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper presents URED, a training-free system that recycles items scored highly by recommenders but never shown to users, reintroducing them at the recall stage of Taobao feed recommendation. Online A/B tests report a 3.47% increase in discovered categories and an 8.47% gain in content richness, with engagement preserved. Ablation studies indicate that both the 30-day aggregation window and score-based filtering are necessary for the gains. ★★★★ Notable: The authors recycle high-scored unexposed candidates instead of boosting discovery exposure, reporting Taobao online A/B tests with gains in discovered categories and richness.

entry.title: Decoupling Pretrained Knowledge for Reuse in Time Series Forecasting Models
entry.summary: Decouple to Reuse: Fine-Grained Knowledge Augmentation for Time Series Foundation Models arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper addresses the difficulty of adapting pretrained time series foundation models to downstream tasks because of domain shifts. It proposes FKA, a two-stage framework that decouples pretraining knowledge into compact, task-shared residual codebooks for trend and seasonal signals, and uses them to augment frozen models. Experiments on eight real-world benchmarks with four backbone models report better effectiveness and efficiency, and show that the codebooks transfer across backbones. ★★★★ Notable: The authors decouple trend and seasonal signals into residual codebooks for retrieval augmentation of frozen TSFMs, reporting experiments on eight benchmarks with four backbones and cross-backbone tra

entry.title: Routes of Reasoning: Controlling Overthinking in MoE Models at Test Time
entry.summary: Routes of Reasoning: Reading and Reshaping Test-Time Compute in MoE Models arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper examines whether the routers in Mixture-of-Experts models reveal the behaviors a model uses during reasoning, such as planning, verifying, and concluding. The authors label reasoning traces by behavior and show that router signals predict these labels nearly as well as residual-stream probes while using fewer features. They then edit expert router scores during inference to reduce overthinking. Across four models and four benchmarks, the median reduction in generated tokens is 30.4%, with accuracy dropping by no more than 0.5 percentage points. ★★★★ Notable: The authors use MoE router scores as a training-free handle on reasoning behaviors, reporting a 30.4% median token reduction across four models and four benchmarks.

entry.title: Does a trial simulator understand what the drug does? An intervention-blind test on 7,207 trials
entry.summary: Does Your Trial Simulator Know What the Drug Does? An Intervention-Blind Test of Interventional Validity on 7,207 Registered Trials arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper proposes a measurement of whether patient world models can truly simulate the effect of an intervention in clinical trials. The authors build 9,996 audited within-trial contrasts from 30,119 phase 2/3 trials with posted results on ClinicalTrials.gov, and compare each simulator against an intervention-blind reference model to score how much its accuracy depends on knowing the tested intervention. A gradient-boosting simulator trained on registry data has negative interventional skill, while a frontier language model reading only the registered protocol scores 0.20, and smaller models sit near the limit of detection. ★★★★ Notable: The authors measure counterfactual skill of patient world models via an intervention-blind reference across 9,996 contrasts from 7,207 trials.

entry.title: Convergence Study of Gradient Temporal-Difference Learning with Regularized Corrections and Eligibility Traces
entry.summary: On Convergence of Gradient Temporal-Difference Learning with Regularized Corrections and Eligibility Traces arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies convergence of temporal-difference (TD) learning, a core reinforcement learning method, for TDRC(λ), a regularized-correction variant. The authors prove convergence under diminishing stepsizes and non-i.i.d. off-policy data, with state-dependent and history-dependent λ parameters. They also propose TDRC(λ)-Huber, which reduces sensitivity to large Bellman errors while keeping the same fixed point. When the mean TD matrix is positive stable, both constrained algorithms converge under sufficiently strong regularization without requiring positive definiteness. ★★★★ Notable: The authors extend TDRC convergence theory to eligibility traces and non-i.i.d. off-policy data, and propose a Huber-based variant with stability analysis.

entry.title: Self-supervised learning of shared latent spaces for neural operators (a reusable function representation trained without labels)
entry.summary: Self-Supervised Learning of Universal Latent Spaces for Operator Learning arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper pre-trains a functional autoencoder on synthesized analytic functions, with no solver or labels, to represent functions on arbitrary point clouds. The resulting latent space is frozen and reused across tasks, so neural operators train on cached embeddings. Across 28 tasks in fluid dynamics, solid mechanics, acoustics, Helmholtz and Poisson equations, the authors report accuracy that can exceed end-to-end architectures, with higher throughput and lower memory use. ★★★★ Notable: The authors decouple representation and operator learning via a self-supervised frozen latent space, reporting gains over end-to-end models on 28 PDE tasks with large memory savings.

entry.title: Male abstraction bias: how abstract concepts link to men in internet culture and AI language models
entry.summary: The Male Abstraction Bias in Internet Culture and Large Language Models arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper examines tens of thousands of single and multi-word expressions across internet text and images, finding that more abstract concepts are more associated with men. The pattern replicates across languages and extends to grammar, with verbs and adverbs being more abstract and more male-coded. The bias also appears in free association responses from both humans and AI, suggesting it is both internalized and reproduced algorithmically. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report that abstractness and male association link across concept space, grammar, and AI free-association, replicated across languages using large internet corpora and images.

entry.title: Can language models tell which constraints should be grouped together?
entry.summary: Do Language Models Know Which Constraints Belong Together? arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper studies how to choose which groups of constraint families to convexify in a mixed-integer program, where some families strengthen the linear relaxation only when applied together. The authors prove that methods observing only bounds need many evaluations to find such hidden groups, and propose JointDW, which combines language-model predictions with a staged search and a one-pass lookahead. On MIPLIB-NL models, the strongest language models identify these groups about as often as the lookahead, and reasoning roughly doubles accuracy. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove a covering-number lower bound for finding hidden constraint groups and test a staged search with language-model predictions on MIPLIB-NL models.

entry.title: VIPBench: A Benchmark for Matching Speaker Models to How Listeners Hear Voice Identity
entry.summary: VIPBench: A Human-Aligned Benchmark for Voice Identity Perception in the Age of Voice Cloning arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper introduces VIPBench, a benchmark built from 124,876 same-or-different judgments by 1,290 listeners on 9,800 recording pairs from 100 public figures, including real recordings, text-to-speech voice clones, and morphs. It defines four tasks for measuring how well speaker-representation models align with human identity perception. Evaluating eleven public speech models, the authors find listeners judged a clone and a real recording of the same speaker to be different people in 41% of responses, and no model reaches the noise ceiling. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors evaluate speaker models against 124,876 human same-or-different judgments on real, cloned, and morphed speech, comparing eleven models.

entry.title: Learning vs. Optimizing Players in Budgeted Games: how a learning agent can resist manipulation and keep low regret when both players face budget constraints
entry.summary: Learning vs. Optimizing Players in Budgeted Games arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies repeated general games over T rounds between a utility-maximizing optimizer and a learning agent, where budget constraints link the players' decisions across rounds. The authors give an efficient, budget-feasible learning algorithm under which any adaptive optimizer earns at most BSE·T+O(√T) in expectation, and the learner has O(√T) regret when the optimizer plays a fixed mixed strategy. The algorithm relies on two novel forms of calibrated forecasts, which can be constructed in polynomial time by simulating online gradient ascent. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give a budget-feasible learner with non-manipulability and low stochastic regret, using two new calibration notions and a polynomial-time forecast construction.

entry.title: Lost in Pooling or Out of Reach? Diagnosing Spatial Left/Right Failures in Vision-Language Similarity
entry.summary: Discarded or Unreachable? Diagnosing and Repairing Spatial Relation Failure in Vision--Language Similarity arXiv · Nov 4, 2026Contrastive vision-language models perform near chance on left/right spatial relations. The paper identifies two causes: the relation may remain in the pooled embedding but be unreachable by native image-text similarity, or pooling may discard it while dense patch features retain it. The authors propose a parameter-free, query-conditioned spatial moment that recomputes geometry from the patch grid and stores it beside the native embedding. On a 118,287-image index it raises left/right pairwise accuracy to 0.81–0.96 while reproducing the native ranking for queries that name no relation. ★★★★ Notable: The authors separate two causes of spatial relation failure and repair both with one readout, reporting gains across ten encoders and a 118,287-image index.

entry.title: Near-Minimax Sample Complexity for Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning under Generative Models
entry.summary: Near-Minimax Sample Complexity for Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning under Generative Models arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies how many samples multi-objective reinforcement learning needs when reward preferences are chosen only after data collection. For finite discounted decision processes with unknown transitions and a generative model, the authors find near-minimax sample complexity that is logarithmic in the number of objectives and saturates at the number of states. Matching lower bounds are also provided, up to logarithmic factors. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors give near-minimax sample complexity for multi-objective RL under generative models, with matching upper and lower bounds up to logarithmic factors.

entry.title: A unified method for combining training datasets and exactly removing their influence from machine learning models
entry.summary: A Unified Framework for Training-Dataset Aggregation and Exact Machine Unlearning via Gibbs Probability Measures arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies three operations on Gibbs probability measures: renormalization, normalized log-linear combination, and nesting, and gives explicit expressions for the objective functions, reference measures, and regularization factors of the resulting measures. When the reference measures are probability measures, these operations are given geometric interpretations involving Pythagorean identities and exponential geodesics. The authors show that nesting and normalized log-linear combination are equivalent, and apply this to Gibbs algorithms so that models trained on local datasets can be combined into models trained on the aggregated data. ★★★★ Notable: The authors unify three Gibbs measure operations, prove nesting equals normalized log-linear combination, and apply this to dataset aggregation and exact unlearning.

entry.title: Tight lower bounds for high-order smooth, uniformly convex minimization
entry.summary: Tight Lower Bounds under Matched High-Order Hölder Smoothness and Uniform Convexity arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper establishes tight lower bounds for minimizing high-order Hölder-smooth and uniformly convex functions when their orders match, i.e., q = p + ν. It shows that any deterministic algorithm using derivatives up to order p needs a number of oracle calls of order Ω of the stated form to reduce an initial optimality gap Δ0 to ε. The bound matches the known upper bound and serves as a higher-order uniformly convex analogue of Nesterov's first-order lower bound for strongly convex functions. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors give a tight lower bound matching the upper bound for matched high-order Hölder smoothness and uniform convexity, via a new multiscale construction.

entry.title: A training-free interface connecting DNA models to frozen language models
entry.summary: A Training-Free Socket for DNA in Frozen Language Models arXiv · Oct 17, 2026This paper introduces socket, a method that links the Evo 2 DNA foundation model to frozen large language models without training a connector. It fits a closed-form ridge regression from DNA features to each host model's representation of gene symbols, names, and descriptions. On the GeneHop five-way multiple-choice benchmark, real DNA outperforms shuffled DNA on all four tested hosts, and the gains survive Holm correction. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report a closed-form ridge plug linking frozen DNA and language models beats shuffled-DNA controls on four hosts.

entry.title: From Pixels to Actions: Toward Native Vision-Language-Action Policies
entry.summary: From Pixels to Actions - Towards Native Vision-Language-Action Policies arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper introduces NEO-VLA, a vision-language-action framework without a separate visual encoder. Images are tokenized by lightweight patch convolutions and evolve jointly with language throughout the backbone, letting an action expert use representations from different depths. Under controlled comparisons, the native design outperforms encoder-based models, and layer-wise probing shows action-critical signals often peak before the final visual layer. The approach yields stronger and more robust control across manipulation tasks and distribution shifts.

entry.title: A framework for adding context to AI social agents while keeping their behavior stable
entry.summary: A Framework for Context Enrichment and Selective Robustness in LLM Social Agents arXiv · Nov 5, 2026Researchers use large language models as agents in social simulations, but these agents often change behavior when prompts are reworded without changing their meaning. The paper introduces controlled context enrichment, which systematically adds neutral padding, generic social background, descriptive decision grounding, or normative decision grounding to prompts. It also proposes selective robustness as a validation criterion: insensitivity to meaning-preserving prompt changes combined with a directional response to decision-relevant social changes. The framework is demonstrated in a Prisoner's Dilemma-like game, where different forms of enrichment produce distinct behavior patterns that vary between the two models tested.

entry.title: FlowReconBench: Benchmark Comparing Learned and Classical Methods for Rebuilding Flow Fields from Sparse Sensors
entry.summary: FlowReconBench: Accuracy, calibration and cost of learned and classical flow reconstruction from sparse sensors arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper presents FlowReconBench, a benchmark that evaluates ten learned and five classical methods for reconstructing full flow fields from sparse sensor data. The methods are tested on a laminar cylinder wake, two-dimensional Kolmogorov turbulence, and three-dimensional isotropic turbulence, using accuracy, calibration, spectra, and computational cost as criteria. The results show that the best-performing method depends on the regime, with classical methods excelling in low-order and dense-sensing cases and data-driven methods performing better when sensor density is low or observability is poor.

entry.title: BEAKER: An Expert-Curated Benchmark for Embodied AI Brains in Self-Driving Chemistry Labs
entry.summary: BEAKER: An Expert-Curated Benchmark for Embodied Brains in Self-Driving Chemical Laboratories arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper introduces BEAKER, a benchmark for testing how well multimodal large language models can act as embodied decision-making systems in self-driving chemical laboratories. It contains 1,000 question-answer samples across 11 image and video task types, all manually written and reviewed by chemistry and AI experts. The authors evaluated 28 models and found they can follow coarse experimental procedures in videos but struggle with precise action grounding, fine-grained equipment and safety recognition, and ordering steps in mid-length procedures.

entry.title: Motion-Guided Contrastive Regularization for Latent World Models
entry.summary: Motion-guided Contrastive Regularization For Latent World Models arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper addresses static collapse, a failure in JEPA-style latent world models where the encoder keeps episode-specific static background while suppressing manipulation-relevant state changes. On OGBench-Cube, randomized backgrounds substantially degrade planning performance. The proposed method uses optical-flow similarities as soft contrastive targets, combined with latent prediction and SIGReg. Reported planning success rises from 52% to 78% on OGBench-Cube with randomized backgrounds and from 14% to 54% on LIBERO-Object.

entry.title: Occlusion for Free: detecting pedestrian occlusion without occlusion labels by comparing two monocular distance cues.
entry.summary: Occlusion for Free: Detecting Occlusion from the Disagreement Between Two Monocular Distance Cues arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper proposes a training-free method that flags occluded pedestrians by comparing the ordering of apparent box height and monocular metric depth, which are pulled apart when an occluder is in front. It needs no focal length or occlusion annotations and reports AUC 0.909 on KITTI for heavy occlusion. It also reports AUC 0.819 on synthetic CARLA scenes, against 0.644 for distance alone.

entry.title: Procedural Adversarial Learning: Training and testing vision models on hard cases found by a controllable scene generator
entry.summary: Procedural Adversarial Learning arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper introduces procedural adversarial learning (PAL), which searches the control parameters of an interpretable procedural image generator to find difficult scenes for minimax training and adversarial evaluation. It proposes the Simple-PAT algorithm, which uses zeroth-order optimization to create adversarial training samples on demand, and releases PAL-Dojo, a set of procedural generators for surface normal estimation, image segmentation, and human pose estimation. Against a cross-model black-box adversary with 50M queries, Simple-PAT reduces worst-case error by a geometric mean of 3.15x over standard training and 2.63x over the strongest robust training baseline.

entry.title: Adaptive Multi Mode: routing black-box optimizers under a budget using online landscape probes
entry.summary: Adaptive Multi Mode: Budget-Aware Routing of Optimizers By Online Landscape Probes arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper introduces AMM, which routes a fixed evaluation budget among five classical optimizers (quasi-Newton, trust-region, coordinate, multistart, evolution-strategy) using online probes of landscape features such as curvature and separability. Tested once on held-out bbob instances against up to seven competitors, AMM had the highest target share in 382 of 600 function-dimension-budget cells. The authors released it as an open-source Python package.

entry.title: SpecCompact: Speeding Up Context Compaction for LLM Agents with Parallel Draft-and-Verify Summaries
entry.summary: SpecCompact: Accelerating LLM Agent Context Compaction with Slot-Parallel Semantic Speculative Verification arXiv · Nov 5, 2026LLM agents compress growing interaction histories, but summarizing long histories with large models adds significant delay. SpecCompact speeds this up by having a small fine-tuned drafter generate structured summary slots in parallel, while the target model verifies each line and repairs rejected content. Across AppWorld and τ³ benchmarks with two target models, it achieves 2.04 to 5.63 times faster compaction than Hermes-style summarization. A user study within Hermes reports a median compaction speedup of 8.68 times.

entry.title: Learning to decode linear error-correcting codes with a neural network based on belief propagation
entry.summary: Learning to Decode Linear Codes with Generalized Belief Propagation Network arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper proposes a Generalized Belief Propagation Network (GBPNet) for decoding linear error-correcting codes. It keeps message-passing symmetry and the Tanner graph structure while adding cascaded variable-node updates and learned element-wise message scaling. Two training strategies, progressive training and high-SNR training, are introduced to improve decoding accuracy. Experiments on several linear codes report lower bit error rates than conventional belief propagation and the evaluated state-of-the-art neural decoders.

entry.title: PixelSpline: continuous video upscaling in space and time using shared pixel motion paths
entry.summary: PixelSpline: Continuous Space-Time Video Super-Resolution via Endpoint-Anchored Shared Pixel Trajectories arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper presents a framework for continuous space-time video super-resolution that combines long-context encoding, continuous high-resolution feature lifting, and an endpoint-anchored module called PixelSpline. PixelSpline models each pixel's motion as one continuous trajectory shared by both endpoint frames, and uses it to warp endpoint colors into a coarse intermediate frame and align high-resolution features for residual reconstruction. Experiments across spatial and temporal upsampling settings show the method offers a favorable quality-efficiency trade-off.

entry.title: Turn-level best-of-N sampling to improve LLM agents on long tasks
entry.summary: On Turn-Level Best-of-N Sampling for Scaling LLM Agents arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper evaluates a inference-time scaling method for LLM agents on complex, long-horizon tasks. At each turn, a generator model proposes N candidate actions and a selector model chooses one to execute in the environment. Experiments on long-horizon terminal tasks report accuracy gains of 5 to 10 percent and better consistency across repeated attempts.

entry.title: CounterFactual Retrieval: An Evidence-Aware Evaluation Method for Identifying Individual Animals
entry.summary: CounterFactual Retrieval for Evidence-Aware Individual Animal Identification arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper argues that current evaluations of individual animal identification report only retrieval accuracy, which does not reveal whether a model relies on animal features or identity-correlated shortcuts. The authors propose Counterfactual Foreground Retrieval (CFR), which evaluates the same query-gallery task using full-image, foreground-only, and shortcut-only views. They also release around 0.5M masks for 34 datasets along with code for mask generation and CFR evaluation.

entry.title: Trade-offs between hierarchical representations and quantization in text embeddings
entry.summary: Balancing hierarchical representation and quantization: A performance trade-off in text embeddings arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This empirical benchmark study examines how two existing techniques, hierarchical text embeddings with variable-length representations and quantization that lowers numerical precision, interact. The authors evaluate 38 tasks from the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark using four transformer-based embedding models. Int8 quantization is statistically indistinguishable from float32 for pair classification and re-ranking, while binary quantization is significantly worse across all task categories. Retrieval degrades much faster than other categories.

entry.title: CompressionBench: Can coding agents compress large language models?
entry.summary: CompressionBench: How can your coding agents compress LLMs? arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper introduces CompressionBench, which frames LLM compression as a terminal task where agents receive a checkpoint, storage limit, inference environment, and time budget, then build compressed weights and executable inference code. Across six agents and six model-size settings, 29 of 36 submissions passed independent verification. The best per-task designs average a 3.4% perplexity increase over BF16 and 77.33% downstream accuracy, versus 79.56% for BF16.

entry.title: LongBanana: An Expert-Verified Benchmark for Multi-Reference Image Synthesis
entry.summary: LongBanana: An Expert-Verified Benchmark for Long-Context Multi-Reference Image Synthesis arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper introduces LongBanana, an expert-designed and expert-verified benchmark for long-context image synthesis from multiple reference images. It contains 90 tasks and 4,670 atomic evaluation items, scored on content fidelity, relational binding, and global constraint satisfaction using an entity-relation graph. The authors also present LongBanana-Gen, an agent-harness framework, and report that a ReAct-Plan-Exec-Reflect workflow yields gains that depend on the harness.

entry.title: Visual Token Routing: a method for keeping only the image tokens that matter
entry.summary: Visual Token Routing: Learning to keep tokens that matter arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper introduces Visual Token Routing (VTR), a training framework for computer-use agents that decides which visual tokens from screenshots are passed to the language model. A lightweight spatio-temporal router, trained jointly with the vision-language model, selects image regions from the current and previous screenshots. The authors report that after 2,000 training steps, VTR matches full-resolution performance on OSWorld, CUA-World, and video game action prediction while using 2.5 to 5.8 times fewer visual tokens.

entry.title: Trainspotting: Learning 3D Object Reconstruction from Scattered Online Photos
entry.summary: Trainspotting: Learning Object-Centric 3D Reconstruction from Found Photos arXiv · Nov 5, 2026Current feedforward 3D reconstruction models perform poorly on object photo collections taken in the wild, since they are mainly trained on single-session captures. This paper introduces Trainspotting, a dataset of 12,068 objects and 311,886 photos from Wikimedia Commons, with recovered camera poses, depth, and object masks. Objects are grouped into fixed-site, moving, and shared-design regimes, and the models fail most severely on the latter two. Fine-tuning VGGT-Ω on this dataset improves pose, depth, and geometry on held-out objects, with similar gains on the NAVI benchmark.

entry.title: Persona Perspectives: How Adopting Viewpoints Reshapes LLM Internal Representations
entry.summary: Persona Perspectives: Adopting Viewpoints Reorganizes Representations in LLMs arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper examines whether prompting a large language model to adopt a political persona, such as liberal or conservative, changes the geometry of its internal representations. The authors compare representations of over 9,000 words across 33 semantic axes under two political personas and two neutral baselines. They find that persona conditioning systematically shifts how words project onto semantic axes, and classifiers trained without a persona yield politically slanted truthfulness and morality ratings when applied to persona-conditioned models.

entry.title: How to Handle Conflicting Criteria for Judging Whether AI Explanations Are Faithful
entry.summary: Navigating Disagreement Among Criteria for Evaluating Explanation Faithfulness arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper examines why existing criteria for evaluating whether algorithmic explanations faithfully reflect a model's behavior can reach conflicting verdicts on the same explanation. The authors introduce a faithfulness functional that locates these disagreements in what an explanation claims, which comparisons support that claim, and how agreement across comparisons is aggregated, and they reconstruct existing criteria within it. A case study of adverse action notices shows how a specific setting can justify some evaluation choices while leaving others open.

entry.title: Where to Connect: DGP, a method that lets multimodal LLMs dynamically choose visual layers via gated pathways
entry.summary: Where to Connect? Boosting MLLMs via Dynamic Gated Pathways across ALL ViT and LLM Layers arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper proposes DGP (Dynamic Gated Pathways), which creates all-to-all connections between every ViT layer and every LLM layer, with each LLM layer dynamically gating its preference over visual layers based on its own semantic state. Built on LLaVA-1.5-7B and 13B, DGP improves over the 7B baseline on several benchmarks and surpasses prior multi-layer visual fusion methods on most. Layer-wise routing analyses show that different LLM layers select different visual granularities on demand.

entry.title: Predicting grain growth in polycrystalline materials under changing temperatures with neural networks
entry.summary: Thermally Conditioned Time-Series Forecasting of Grain Growth in Polycrystalline Materials arXiv · Nov 5, 2026Grain growth during heat treatment affects the microstructure and mechanical properties of polycrystalline materials. This work extends a previous forecasting framework, which worked only under constant temperature, to non-isothermal conditions by combining a convolutional network for grain size distributions, a multilayer perceptron for thermal inputs, and a recurrent network for temporal prediction. The model is trained and evaluated on data from validated front-tracking simulations across diverse non-isothermal thermal paths. It reproduces grain growth dynamics under complex thermal histories with high accuracy.

entry.title: Same Layout, Different Count: How Number Words Behave Above Ten in Text-to-Image Models
entry.summary: Same Layout, Different Count: What Number Words Do Past Ten in Text-to-Image Models arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies whether number words control object counts in five open text-to-image models when requests exceed about ten objects. Holding the object and starting noise fixed, the authors changed one condition at a time and had people count 3,088 images. Models follow small numbers, but their adherence weakens past a limit, and the number word does not reliably steer the count in a consistent direction.

entry.title: Before You Continue: Checking if AI Chat Assistants Remember Time-Based Safety Limits
entry.summary: Before You Continue: Evaluating Time-Sensitive Safety Awareness in Conversational Assistants arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper introduces TASC, a benchmark that tests whether large language model assistants apply time-dependent constraints when answering conversational requests. It includes 3,418 inputs built from 128 templates, plus 33 scenarios comparing elapsed-time calculation with applying that information. Across 13 models, assistants considered time-dependent constraints in only 30.5% of cases where the proposed action violated a rule, and in 62.1% of cases they failed to apply constraints even when they calculated the elapsed time correctly.

entry.title: Context-aware image generation that adapts its order to reason better
entry.summary: Context-Aware Autoregressive Image Generation for Emerging Reasoning Properties arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper proposes a context-aware autoregressive image generation framework that dynamically chooses the next token location based on global context and current local information, instead of using a fixed or random order. Experiments show improved structural robustness across masked autoregressive and scale-wise autoregressive models.
