The authors also report that the approach helps models better understand complex semantic instructions and produce images that follow them more faithfully.

entry.title: Predicting LLM answer activations from context before the first answer token
entry.summary: Context--Answer Metamodels: Forecasting LLM Activations Before the First Answer Token arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper studies how a single context can produce many different language model answers under stochastic decoding, which normally requires costly rollouts. The authors train context–answer metamodels that map context activations to point or distribution forecasts of mean-pooled answer activations. The four metamodel families forecast these activations with high fidelity, improve up to 500,000 training prompts, and generalize zero-shot to out-of-domain data. Forecasts retain behavior-predictive signal and transfer from Qwen2.5 to Qwen3.5 and Gemma 4.

entry.title: LooM: Loop-Invariant Memory for Efficient Looped Transformer Language Models
entry.summary: LooM: Loop-Invariant Memory for Causal Encoder-Decoder Language Models arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper proposes LooM (Loop-invariant Memory), a method for looped Transformers that addresses memory growth with loop count, coarse compute adjustment, and difficulty changing loops after training. In a causal encoder-decoder, only the decoder layers after the first are looped, reading a global memory written once per token, and key-value entries are published only on the first visit so the cache does not grow. One model trained on randomly sampled budgets supports every budget from 3 to 21 layer executions per token without a router. With enough loops, LooM outperforms a single-pass baseline trained on the same data at the same cache size.

entry.title: Alignment Myopia in Generative AI: a paper arguing current AI alignment ignores long-term effects on people and should shift toward long-horizon alignment.
entry.summary: Alignment Myopia in Generative AI arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper argues that current generative AI alignment relies on short-horizon feedback that prioritizes immediate conversational satisfaction. It contends this overlooks long-term effects of persistent human-AI interaction, such as cognitive atrophy, social erosion, and diminished human agency. The authors map tensions between near-term utility and long-term costs across four facets of human well-being and advocate alignment strategies that actively foster long-term well-being beyond simple preference optimization.

entry.title: Developing AWS Cloud FPGA Designs with High-Level Vitis HLS
entry.summary: Enabling AWS Cloud FPGA Development Using High-Level Vitis HLS arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper presents a toolchain for developing machine learning models on AWS EC2 F2 cloud FPGAs from high-level code, connecting Vitis HLS to the HDK and AFI workflow. It introduces a four-level methodology for localizing errors, including FPGA-specific circuit errors. The authors validate the approach by implementing the embedding layer and the first of four encoder layers of a TinyBERT address Named Entity Recognition model on FPGA hardware. Weights are streamed from host DRAM, and performance is weaker than CPU and GPU implementations.

entry.title: Systolic Linear Attention: A TPU-Tailored Gated Delta Attention Design
entry.summary: Systolic Linear Attention: Co-Designing Tile-Grouped Gated Delta Attention for TPUs arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper redesigns gated delta linear attention layers, which were originally tuned for GPUs, to better fit Google TPU hardware. The proposed Systolic Linear Attention (SLA) widens keys to 256, groups value heads and decay gates, and computes chunk solves in one fused kernel. The authors report that on TPU v7x, SLA layers run 1.6x to 2.5x faster than the open-source Tokamax KDA kernel, and train 11% to 24% faster than KDA in large MoE pre-training at similar perplexity.

entry.title: Training and calibration data for open models on ARC-AGI-2 puzzles
entry.summary: Rules, Traces and Routing Statistics: Training and Calibration Data for Open Models on ARC-AGI-2 arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper studies which training and calibration data help three open models solve ARC-AGI-2 tasks under offline, four-GPU, 12-hour limits. For the NVARC Qwen3-4B model, continued fine-tuning on 1,920 real task records raised the semi-private score from 28.96 to 33.06 (mean of five runs), outperforming checkpoints trained on synthetic tasks. For Qwen3.8-27B, combining fine-tuning on its own correct reasoning traces with an improved inference procedure raised the score from 26.81 to 44.03, with most of the gain attributed to the inference procedure.

entry.title: Open-HumanScale: An Open Recipe for Scaling Human and Robot Experience for Embodied Foundation Models
entry.summary: Open-HumanScale: An Open Recipe for Scaling Human and Robot Experience for Embodied Foundation Models arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper presents Open-HumanScale, a fully open recipe for scaling egocentric human video pretraining to 50,000 hours, along with the dense hand-motion and language-annotated corpus Open-HumanScale-50K. The authors report an empirical log-linear relationship between pretraining data hours and downstream robot success rates. They build HumanWAM-Vanilla, pretrained only on human video, and HumanWAM-Goal, pretrained with joint human-robot data, and report results on RoboTwin 2.0 and RoboDojo benchmarks. Data, pipelines, checkpoints, and evaluation suites are open-sourced.

entry.title: SAUCE: A Fact-Based Method for Checking Conversation Summaries
entry.summary: SAUCE: Summary Analysis Using Conversation Entailment arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper introduces SAUCE, a reference-free, fact-based pipeline for evaluating cross-lingual summaries of conversational speech. It measures summary accuracy and fact coverage by checking entailment between the conversation and the summary text. Unlike black-box LLM evaluators or dense embedding metrics, SAUCE maps scores to discrete, verifiable facts, so exact hallucinations or omissions can be identified. Preliminary investigations show that its results align strongly with human judgment.

entry.title: Evolving interpretable spatial descriptors to uncover structure-property links
entry.summary: Evolutionary Design of Interpretable Spatial Descriptors for Structure-Property Relationship Discovery arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper presents a framework for building spatial descriptors that predict local spectra and hysteresis loops from images. The authors benchmark regression models, use SHAP maps to examine spatial attribution, and study how patch size and compression affect accuracy and descriptor dimensionality. A genetic algorithm is then used to optimize spatial partitions and the choice of mean, minimum, and maximum pooling, with Cartesian and polar constructions compared.

entry.title: LLMs Don't Know What They Know: A Benchmark for Testing Whether Models Can Judge Their Own Knowledge Dates in Financial Backtests
entry.summary: LLMs Don't Know What They Know: Benchmarking Temporal Self-Knowledge for Financial Backtesting arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper introduces FinDendro, a benchmark of 2,226 dated U.S. facts from 1999 to 2026, including macroeconomic series, month-end stock prices and Federal Reserve decisions, to test whether language models accurately judge what they know. For most frontier models, self-reports understate actual knowledge; for example, GPT-5 answers 76% of controlled facts correctly but claims to know only 38%. The authors conclude that self-report, instructions, or stated knowledge cutoffs cannot certify that a backtest within a model's training window is free of leaked outcomes.

entry.title: Measuring Risk, Not Harm: Detecting Signs of Psychological Harm Risk in AI Chats
entry.summary: Measuring Risk, Not Harm: Detecting Psychological Harm Risk Factors in LLM Conversations arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper proposes monitoring psychological harm from large language models by detecting observable risk-factor behaviors in AI responses rather than measuring harm directly. The authors define eight such behaviors and build a synthetic multi-label corpus of 47,062 AI responses. They compare embedding-based classifiers, direct LLM judging, and a classifier-judge cascade, with the best cascade reaching an F1 of 0.79 on held-out human-labeled data.

entry.title: Efficient Agent Evaluation Using Cached Execution Traces
entry.summary: Task-Efficient Agent Evaluation Using Cached Traces arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper proposes estimating an AI agent system's full benchmark score from only a few task executions. Each execution trace is summarized by an LLM and embedded with a text encoder, preserving correctness- and task-related signals. On SWE-bench Verified and Terminal-Bench 2.0, mean absolute error drops from 0.13 to 0.08 and from 0.14 to 0.12 when only one random task is executed.

entry.title: ConDR: Conservative Reachability via Neural Hamilton-Jacobi Subsolutions
entry.summary: ConDR: Conservative Reachability through Neural Hamilton-Jacobi Subsolutions arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper addresses safety reachability analysis for dynamical systems, where DeepReach can misclassify truly unsafe states as safe. The authors propose Conservative DeepReach (ConDR), which learns a subsolution of the Hamilton-Jacobi-Isaacs variational inequality so that the learned unsafe set contains the true one, and prove its value lies within ε·τ of the true value function. Compared with DeepReach and MADR on Air3D, Air6D, a 9D multi-vehicle system, and a 13D quadrotor, ConDR reports the lowest misclassification and closed-loop collision rates.

entry.title: Message-passing graph persistence: topological descriptors that incorporate GNN message passing
entry.summary: Message-passing graph persistence arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper introduces Message-Passing Graph Persistence (MGP), a family of topological descriptors that integrates message passing into graph filtrations. At each filtration step, node embeddings are updated on the current subgraph and linked to persistence events, and they also determine representatives of connected components. The authors prove MGP is invariant under graph isomorphism and strictly more expressive than the persistent homology descriptors it extends. Experiments on an expressivity benchmark and several graph classification and regression datasets show MGP outperforms other PH-based descriptors on most of them.

entry.title: VA-TDM: A unified framework improving few-step diffusion models via velocity adversarial distillation
entry.summary: VA-TDM: A Unified View for Improving Few-Step Diffusion Models by Velocity Adversarial Distillation arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper introduces Velocity Adversarial Distillation (VAD), which uses a learned critic to compare velocity fields of a student and teacher model and turns their disagreement into training feedback. Building on it, VA-TDM provides supervision for partial denoising along the student's trajectory. The method achieves state-of-the-art four-step results in text-to-image and text-to-video generation across several backbones and scales to a 33B MiniMax-H3 model.

entry.title: Turning integer grids into spatial intuition: perception, not planning, drives ARC-AGI-3 performance
entry.summary: Transforming Integer Grids to Spatial Intuition: Perception, Not Planning, Governs ARC-AGI-3 arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper presents SARBLOH, an open-weight agent for ARC-AGI-3, a benchmark of uninstructed visual games. Its zero-parameter perception engine converts each frame into an object inventory, a geometric briefing, and an annotated canvas, and the agent writes code to express hypotheses. The authors report that across eight presentations the rubric score rose from 3/28 to 25/28 while token use fell by 89.4%.

entry.title: Whether Two Paper Acceptance Predictors Agree on Which Paragraph Edits Raise Scores
entry.summary: Ranking Agreement Does Not Reveal Paragraph-Edit Agreement in Two Released Paper Acceptance Predictors arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper compares a fast classifier with two released text-only paper acceptance predictors on 198 ICLR papers and their paragraph rewrites. The classifier agrees with the predictors on ranking original papers, but shows no detectable agreement on which rewrites raise scores. A full-precision re-check gives the same result, with only a tiny average gain over random choice. The authors recommend checking revision selectors against the intended evaluator on the revisions they rank.

entry.title: FedFiOT: Fisher-weighted optimal transport for merging models in one-shot and few-round federated learning
entry.summary: FedFiOT: Fisher-Weighted Optimal Transport for Model Merging in One-Shot and Few-Round Federated Learning arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper addresses problems in one-shot and few-round federated learning, where client models drift apart and neurons become misaligned. It proposes FedFiOT, which uses Fisher information to weigh parameter importance and guide neuron alignment and aggregation. The method jointly optimizes neuron correspondences and global parameters by alternating minimization of a shared Fisher-weighted objective. The authors report consistent improvements over baselines across multiple datasets in both settings.

entry.title: Semantic Residual Vector Quantization for Sign Language Generation (paper)
entry.summary: Semantic Residual Vector Quantization for Sign Language Generation arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper proposes Semantic Residual Vector Quantization (SRVQ), a framework that generates sign language motion from written sentences in two stages. It first encodes the sign content at a semantic level, then refines pose, handshape, trajectory, and body coordination in later residual levels. On CSL-Daily and Phoenix-2014T, the authors report R@1 scores of 82.3 and 70.3, respectively, which they say exceed the previous state of the art by 30 and 46 points.

entry.title: A benchmark testing whether AI models can spot fine details in drone images for city management.
entry.summary: Benchmarking Fine-Grained Visual Reasoning for Remote Sensing in Urban Management arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper introduces UMBench, a fine-grained urban remote sensing benchmark built from UAV images for tasks such as traffic monitoring, urban construction, environmental quality, and disaster warning. Evaluations show that current multimodal large language models often rely on scene-level priors and overlook fine-grained visual evidence. The authors propose a training-free, evidence-first chain-of-thought method that directs models to inspect such evidence. Experiments report that this method improves the performance of both open-source and commercial models on UMBench.

entry.title: Route First, See Later: separating routing policy from action spaces so vision agents reason scientifically
entry.summary: Route First, See Later: Enabling Vision Agents to Reason Scientifically by Separating Routing Policy from Action Spaces arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper introduces ZETA, an architecture that separates routing policy from action execution in vision agents for scientific image analysis, so routing errors and execution failures can be evaluated independently. On a zero-shot benchmark of 51 scientific-intent queries, explicit routing semantics substantially improved routing accuracy, especially at semantically adjacent action boundaries, though gains varied across models. The authors report that for Qwen 3.8, segmentation routing accuracy rose from 6.2% to 75.0% and detection routing accuracy from 60.0% to 100%.

entry.title: Continual Classification Beyond the Kernel Regime: Using L2 Regularization's Sparsity Bias in Diagonal Linear Networks
entry.summary: Continual Classification Beyond the Kernel Regime: Harnessing the Sparsity Bias of L2 Regularization in Diagonal Linear Networks arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies continual logistic regression with linear predictors in a high-dimensional statistical setting. It derives the optimal L2 regularization strength for continual linear classification and characterizes its generalization performance. Using a minimal two-layer diagonal linear network, it shows that L2 regularization promotes sparse feature learning in single-task settings but loses this sparsity bias in continual learning, and proposes a weighted L2 variant that restores it. The authors report that, for sufficiently sparse teachers, this variant converges substantially faster over moderate task horizons.

entry.title: EvoWorld: Out-of-Sight World Evolution in Generative Video Models
entry.summary: EvoWorld: Towards Out-of-Sight World Evolution in Generative Video Models arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper argues that generative video models render plausible visuals but lack the reasoning needed to determine how events change a world. It defines the Out-of-Sight Causal Evolution problem and proposes EvoWorld, where a vision-language model tracks world state and reasons about consequences while a segment-autoregressive renderer produces the video. The authors also release EvoWorld-Data and EvoWorld-Bench for training and evaluation, and report that EvoWorld improves event-conditioned causal evolution over recent models while preserving visual quality and consistency.

entry.title: TailSteer: A Method to Curb Visual Drift in Multi-turn Image Editing
entry.summary: TailSteer: Trajectory-Tail Steering for Drift-Resistant Multi-turn Image Editing arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper observes that strong single-turn image editing does not ensure reliable multi-turn editing, since small unintended changes accumulate over repeated edits. It proposes TailSteer, a final-stage training framework that aims to reduce this drift while keeping the capabilities learned earlier by the model. Experiments on the FLUX, SenseNova, and Qwen model families report substantially less cumulative drift over 15 to 20 editing turns, with base-model performance largely preserved on benchmarks.

entry.title: Coupled Scene Graph Anticipation: Constrained Recall Can Mask Structural Inconsistency
entry.summary: Coupled Scene Graph Anticipation: When With-Constraint Recall Hides Structural Inconsistency arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper proposes CoupledSGA, a model that predicts object relationships in future video frames by letting relationships sharing an entity influence each other. It adds a Structural Consistency Loss based on mutually exclusive predicates. The authors show that With-Constraint evaluation cannot capture within-group violations, and on Action Genome the loss lowers the No-Constraint contradiction rate from 45.92% to 4.07% while reducing R@20 from 42.21% to 35.18%.

entry.title: Phone-Based VR Exergames That Turn HIIT Workouts into Games with Real-Time Pose Tracking
entry.summary: Smartphone-Aided VR Exergames for HIIT: Gamifying Fitness with Real-Time Pose Estimation arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper presents a VR exergame system that gamifies High-Intensity Interval Training with 11 predefined combo moves. A standard smartphone on a tripod captures full-body movement, which is processed in real time by a pose estimation algorithm and assessed by a backend using MCP and GPT-4o. In a within-subject study of 20 participants aged 18 to 25, VR sessions produced higher enjoyment, immersion, and likelihood to recommend than non-VR sessions. The system's evaluations agreed with a certified trainer's assessments in 87.5% of 10 sessions.

entry.title: ConceptARC at Scale: Testing Concept Understanding in Reasoning Models
entry.summary: ConceptARC at Scale: Studying Conceptual Understanding in Reasoning Models arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper introduces ConceptARC at Scale, a generator that creates thousands of ARC-style tasks targeting specific concepts. Using it, the authors build ConceptARC-100, a dataset of 1,600 manually reviewed tasks covering 16 concepts, ten times the size of the original benchmark. They evaluate recent reasoning models and models trained from scratch, and analyze their internal representations. The representations cluster by operations applied to objects, such as recoloring, removal, or translation, suggesting models form stable abstractions of transformation operations.

entry.title: Reusing output templates to simulate shell command results with small language models
entry.summary: Template Gap Reconstruction for Shell Output Simulation with Small Language Models arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper introduces template gap reconstruction (TGR), a method for simulating shell command output with small language models without executing the commands. A template selector picks a reusable output template, and autoregressive models generate the varying gaps between fixed literals. Evaluated on a target environment excluded from the template bank, TGR improves output edit similarity when template coverage is high and reduces generated tokens by 26.3% to 38.3%.

entry.title: "Turns Matter": Improving Streaming Video Reinforcement Learning with Turn-Level Credit Assignment
entry.summary: Turns Matter: Advancing Streaming Video RL via Turn-Level Credit arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper addresses streaming video understanding, where models must repeatedly decide whether to respond or keep observing. It proposes TurnWise, a turn-level GRPO framework that computes group-relative advantages for each streaming decision from its remaining return. Token losses are averaged within each turn and then across turns, so response and waiting decisions receive equal weight. Experiments show the method outperforms prior RL approaches for streaming video understanding.

entry.title: Airlock: Limiting Fault Spread in Multi-Agent Systems via Selective Online Containment
entry.summary: Airlock: Bounding the Multi-Agent Blast Radius via Selective Online Containment arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper presents Airlock, a runtime and guardrail for multi-agent systems that performs selective fault containment after an alert. Its tree-structured runtime, EdgeCitadel, narrows permissions from parent to child agents, while an append-only provenance graph records cross-agent data consumption. After an alert, Airlock traces forward to isolate tainted executions and pending actions, and backward to identify root causes. An optional optimized cut minimizes disruption to healthy work under a deadline.

entry.title: Survey of dexterous robotic hands in the foundation-model era
entry.summary: Dexterous Robotic Hands in the Foundation-Model Era: A Full-Stack Survey of Hardware, Data, Cross-Embodiment Transfer, Learning, and Evaluation arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This survey reviews research on dexterous robotic hands from January 2024 to early November 2026, including earlier studies to show technical lineages. It organizes the literature into five connected layers: hardware, data collection and curation, cross-embodiment transfer, learning and foundation models, and evaluation and applications. The authors conclude that the value of human data depends on kinematic, visual and contact alignment rather than recording volume alone. They also argue that completing a task is not sufficient to establish physical correctness or deployment readiness.

entry.title: Study of symmetry breaking at the edge of stability using central flow analysis
entry.summary: Symmetry Breaking at the Edge of Stability via Central Flow Analysis arXiv · Nov 5, 2026Neural networks have continuous symmetries that yield quantities conserved under gradient flow, such as layer balancedness in linear and ReLU networks. At the edge of stability, where iterates oscillate around a smoother trajectory described by central flow dynamics, finite-step gradient descent may not preserve these conservation laws. The paper studies how gradient flow conservation laws evolve under this central flow description, analysing a scalar two-layer model, two-layer matrix factorisation, and a two-layer ReLU network to determine which laws remain and which are broken.

entry.title: Reasoning Over Supplied Facts in Multilingual LLMs
entry.summary: Reasoning over Non-Parametric Memory in Multilingual LLMs: A Cognitive-Based Analysis of Relational Knowledge arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper introduces Rel-Bloom, a multilingual diagnostic benchmark of 450 multiple-choice questions built from 30 Wikidata relations. Questions are arranged across five Bloom-inspired levels and three veracity conditions, and 43 models were tested in six languages. Accuracy drops sharply from the Apply to Analyze level in open-weight models, and Evaluate items remain difficult even for strong models. The authors conclude that greater model capability does not by itself guarantee reliable reasoning over supplied relational evidence.

entry.title: Energy-Guided Transport: A Projection-Free Method for Physics-Constrained Flow Matching
entry.summary: Energy-Guided Transport for Projection-Free Physics-Informed Flow Matching arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper proposes Energy-Guided Transport, a training-free framework that expresses nonlinear physical constraints as a smooth potential energy landscape. Instead of interrupting ODE integration with algebraic projections, it applies a continuous dissipative force to intermediate generative states to steer them toward the physical manifold. The method is evaluated on various 1D and 2D physical systems, including the chaotic Navier-Stokes equations.

entry.title: Beyond the Principle-Practice Gap: Responsible AI as a Situated Ethical and Epistemic Practice
entry.summary: Beyond the principle-practice gap: Responsible AI as situated epistemic and ethical practice arXiv · Nov 5, 2026Responsible AI research has found that ethical principles are often not reflected in AI design and development, a gap usually treated as a problem of implementation, awareness, or compliance. Based on fourteen interviews with people designing and governing AI-enabled anti-trafficking systems, this paper argues that the gap arises from institutional and professional conditions that shape which issues actors recognise as ethical problems requiring action. It describes four linked moments: perception, judgement, situated action, and socio-technical materialisation. The authors conclude that responsible AI governance needs epistemic infrastructures that make the knowledge of affected communities receivable and actionable in design.

entry.title: ALTO: A Corpus of Tech-Facilitated Gender-Based Violence in African and Levantine Languages
entry.summary: ALTO: African and Levantine Tech-Facilitated Gender-Based Violence Corpus arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper presents ALTO, a dataset of 3,022 examples of tech-facilitated gender-based violence in Levantine Arabic, African French, and Swahili. The examples were crowdsourced with civil society organizations in Jordan, Francophone West Africa, and Kenya, and annotated using active learning. Existing harmful content detection models show poor recall on ALTO, which improves with fine-tuning, and models often miss covert harms, with markedly higher error rates in Swahili. The annotation taxonomy, dataset, and trained models are released.

entry.title: Where It Breaks: Diagnosing Failures of a Vision-Language Pac-Man Agent
entry.summary: Where It Breaks: Diagnosing Perception, Memory, and Decision Failures of a Vision-Language Agent in Pac-Man arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies a Qwen3.5-9B-based vision-language agent that plays Pac-Man using only four movement actions, asking whether poor performance comes from reading the screen or from choosing actions over long sequences. Using separate perception checks and primitive-policy reinforcement learning on textual boards, completion on eight held-out mazes rose from 0% to 80.2% at a selected checkpoint. The authors find that accurate static screenshot reading can coexist with errors during interaction, and that further optimization can come with worse action choices.

entry.title: Agent-driven generative priors for synthesizing and segmenting pathology images
entry.summary: Agent-Driven Generative Priors for Pathology Image Synthesis and Segmentation arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper proposes a three-stage framework to address the scarcity of pixel-level annotations in pathology images. A pathology agent system screens image quality to build TCGA-200K, a dataset of 217,030 patches from TCGA, and a generative model trained on it is adapted to semantic segmentation with a lightweight head. The authors also introduce PathSeg-380K, with expert annotations for about 380,000 cells across 12 cell types. Experiments on multiple pathology datasets report state-of-the-art segmentation performance.

entry.title: PINR-ESI: A Physics-Informed Self-Supervised Neural Method for Mapping Brain Activity from EEG
entry.summary: PINR-ESI: Physics-Informed Self-Supervised Implicit Neural Representation Framework for EEG Extended-Source Imaging arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper proposes a method for extended-source EEG imaging that requires no paired source labels or simulation-based supervised pretraining. It uses a lead field matrix to constrain an implicit neural representation so that predicted and measured EEG agree, modeling cortical current density as a continuous field. Simulations showed the clearest advantage in identifying multiple and larger active cortical regions. Evaluations on real EEG from epilepsy patients and intracranial stimulation experiments supported the framework's feasibility for source imaging.

entry.title: Adds a Detector-Agnostic Subspace Signal to Improve Near-OOD Detection
entry.summary: Don't Replace, Complement: A Detector-Agnostic Subspace Signal for Near-OOD Detection arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper proposes PLUS, a method for near-out-of-distribution (near-OOD) detection that builds a low-dimensional per-class subspace from a sparse autoencoder's most class-active neurons. Inputs are scored by their whitened squared Mahalanobis distance within the subspace of their predicted class. This signal is fused additively with existing detection scores at a single fixed global weight. Across 18 detectors and 126 detector–backbone combinations, it consistently improves near-OOD AUROC while far-OOD performance is broadly maintained or improved.

entry.title: LifeVal: A Benchmark for Testing AI on Personalized Consumer Tasks
entry.summary: LifeVal: Evaluating AI Model Performance on Personalized Agentic Consumer Tasks arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper introduces LifeVal, a benchmark for evaluating how well AI models handle personalized agentic consumer tasks across 148 categories, such as managing finances, moving apartments, searching for a job, and finding childcare. The authors estimate the tasks' value through a survey of over 3,800 consumers, cross-referenced with the American Time Use Survey and the Multinational Time Use Study. Task creators who met an expertise threshold built the tasks from real ChatGPT conversations, memories, reference files, and personal context, and each task passed at least three rounds of human quality control.

entry.title: Sekai: Incremental Event Memory for Reasoning Video Segmentation That Tracks Changing Targets
entry.summary: Sekai: Incremental Event Memory for Generalized Reasoning Video Segmentation arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper introduces Generalized Reasoning Video Segmentation (GRVS), a task where the objects matching a query can change as new events occur in a video. The authors build Isekai, a benchmark of 60 videos and 197 queries, and propose Sekai, an online framework with an event memory reasoner and a memory-grounded decoder. Sekai reaches 50.33 J&F, improving on the strongest baseline by 3.2 points.

entry.title: SecureGARD: Ontology-Guided Security Framework for Tool-Using AI Agents
entry.summary: SecureGARD: Dynamic Ontology-Guided Governance for Secure Tool-Using LLM Agents arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper presents SecureGARD, a framework that governs large language model agents which call external tools, aiming to block indirect prompt-injection attacks. It maps tool calls to a shared semantic representation and uses an executable ontology to decide whether each action is ready, waiting, or forbidden, with waiting states enabling bounded replanning. The ontology is refined offline from verified training runs and frozen after held-out validation. The authors report a 0% attack success rate on AgentDojo, ASB, and AgentDyn, along with improved task utility under attack.

entry.title: Do unlearning algorithms learn the right features?
entry.summary: Do unlearning algorithms learn the right features? arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper examines how machine unlearning, which removes the influence of deleted training data from a model, is evaluated. The authors argue that comparing only post-deletion outputs can hide differences in the features encoded by an unlearned model versus one retrained on the remaining data. They prove that models agreeing in output can be broken apart by a single gradient step on their prediction heads. They also introduce a feature recovery measure that separates missing from extraneous features, finding that many methods performing well on standard metrics fail to recover the retrained features.

entry.title: Self-Directed Apple Tasting: Online Learning with Partial Feedback
entry.summary: Self-Directed Apple Tasting arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies the classical apple-tasting setting, a partial-feedback model where the learner sees the true label only when it predicts 1. It considers a self-directed variant in which the learner adaptively chooses the order of points to predict on. In the realizable case, the authors establish a tetrachotomy for the expected minimax number of mistakes, with rates depending on the VC dimension, the ∅-centered star number, and the self-directed dimension. In the agnostic case, the minimax regret is either $\tilde \Theta(\sqrt{n})$ or $\Theta(n)$, depending on the VC dimension.

entry.title: AgentTrustCI: Build-Time Tests for Java LLM Agent Policy, Grounding, and Trajectories
entry.summary: AgentTrustCI: Build-Time Policy, Grounding, and Trajectory Tests for Java LLM Agents arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper presents AgentTrustCI, a Java and JUnit 5 framework that checks LLM agents at build time for policy compliance, grounding of answers in tool output, and adherence to required workflows. It applies these checks to recorded traces and was evaluated on 55 synthetic cases, where the full pipeline correctly classified all injected faults and passing controls and missed no critical cases. The authors note that these results reflect coverage of the authored regression suite rather than production accuracy.

entry.title: Finding Where Search Agents Make Mistakes: Graph-Based Step-Level Checking
entry.summary: Where Search Agents Go Off the Rails: Graph-Grounded Step-Level Verification arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies search-augmented reasoning systems that can reach correct answers despite errors in intermediate steps. The authors introduce GraphRail, which represents requirements, evidence, and reasoning as structured claims and compares them without a generative judge or gold answer. Across three multi-hop QA benchmarks and three reasoning frameworks, GraphRail achieves higher error recall than generative verifiers and remains stable under stochastic extraction.

entry.title: Timing analysis to identify dispatchers in distributed model extraction
entry.summary: Fingerprinting the Dispatchers behind Distributed Model Extraction arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper examines how API distillation campaigns spread requests across many load-balanced accounts to evade content classifiers. It shows that request arrival times and stream completion times reveal the underlying dispatching strategy, such as round-robin counters or key-shuffling pools. Using a 20 percent seed set, the timing analysis ranks the remaining accounts of a campaign within 20 minutes with an AUC of 0.92 to 1.00.

entry.title: Beyond Accuracy: What AI Assurance Must Establish in Public Services
entry.summary: Beyond accuracy: what AI assurance needs to establish in public services arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper examines how public bodies can decide whether AI-generated evidence, such as classifications and summaries, is reliable enough to use. The authors tested eight GPT-4o configurations classifying 1,200 UK Prime Minister's Questions into 21 policy topics against human labels and repeated runs. Accuracy was similar across settings, but 24.3% of labels changed between runs and agreement between configurations did not ensure correctness. The authors also analysed 37 UK and EU policy documents on testing and oversight requirements.

entry.title: Detecting hidden robot action errors using calibrated relational world models
entry.summary: Detecting Silent Action-Interface Mismatch with Calibrated Relational World Models arXiv · Nov 5, 2026Robot actions can meet shape and range checks yet still have wrong meaning, such as swapped axes, inverted signs, or reversed gripper polarity. The paper uses learned state-action-effect relations as offline contracts, calibrating alarms on clean held-out transitions and ranking likely faulty fields with a fixed inverse vocabulary. On ten LIBERO Spatial tasks with 432 source episodes, at a 2.5% clean false-positive rate, the exact conditional of a four-component joint Gaussian mixture reached 65.7% recall, versus 46.1% for ridge residuals. These are retrospective diagnostics, not deployment calibration guarantees.

entry.title: Dynamical State-Space Diffusion for Spatiotemporal Prediction
entry.summary: Dynamical State-Space Diffusion for Spatiotemporal Prediction arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper proposes Dynamical State-Space Diffusion (DSSD) for spatiotemporal prediction. Unlike standard diffusion models that add independent noise to each frame, DSSD learns the temporal structure of the noise process itself, building a temporal kernel from damped oscillatory modes of a stable state-space model. The denoiser architecture stays unchanged. On scientific-field and robot-video datasets, DSSD outperforms diffusion baselines that share its denoiser.

entry.title: Reproducibility and robustness of large language models in political and social science research
entry.summary: Replicability, Reproducibility, and Robustness in Political and Social Science Research with Large Language Models arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This chapter examines the reproducibility problem in research using large language models, whose probabilistic outputs vary across models and versions. It proposes a distribution-based standard for replicability, reproducibility, and robustness, along with a standardized prompt script and error-structure analysis. Using three datasets, the authors show that the choice of measurement can reverse the sign of downstream regression coefficients. They also present a stacked ensemble of open-weight models that improves precision in the correction step while retaining estimate validity.

entry.title: Predicting human motion by progressively compensating for lost prior knowledge
entry.summary: Human Motion Prediction via Continual Prior Compensation arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper addresses human motion prediction, which forecasts future human poses from observed past motion sequences. The authors propose Continual Prior Compensation (CPC), a framework that splits predictions for different time horizons into subtasks trained in multiple stages, with a learnable Prior Compensation Factor measuring prior knowledge loss. An extended version, CPC++, adds a Fine-Grained Prior Compensation Factor for each subtask. Experiments on three benchmark datasets with several state-of-the-art backbone models show the frameworks are effective and flexible.

entry.title: Uncertainty-guided efficient communication for drones sharing sensor data
entry.summary: Uncertainty-Driven Efficient Communication for UAV-Based Collaborative Perception arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper proposes UCP, a framework that makes communication efficient for UAV teams sharing perception data. It uses observational uncertainty to find sensor-limited regions and discriminative uncertainty to find ambiguous regions near the decision boundary, generating request and supply maps. Received messages are fused by U-Fusion, an uncertainty-guided cross-attention module. Experiments on three benchmarks cover 3D object detection and trajectory prediction.

entry.title: TestBED: An Open-Source Toolkit for Bayesian Experimental Design
entry.summary: TestBED: An Open-Source Toolkit for Bayesian Experimental Design arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper presents TestBED, a general-purpose open-source toolkit for Bayesian experimental design (BED). It breaks the BED process into modular, reusable components covering tasks, objectives, training, policy architectures, and evaluation, along with scalable implementations of core primitives such as expected information gain estimators. The authors use TestBED to run a large-scale benchmark of contemporary BED methods, including controlled studies of design policy choices such as time embeddings.

entry.title: Trick-or-Treat: Adversarial Testing of Medical AI Using Synthetic Images
entry.summary: Trick-or-Treat: Adversarial Evaluation of Multimodal Medical Reasoning with Synthetic Images arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper introduces Trick-or-Treat, a benchmark that pairs real chest radiographs with synthetic clinical photographs to test whether models reason correctly across image types. In mismatched pairs, three frontier models hallucinated clinically significant photograph findings 45-57.5% of the time, compared with 25-37.5% when the photographs were shown alone. The models tended to ignore the mismatch and invent findings that fit the radiograph instead.

entry.title: From Certified Pairs to a Certified Hub: Checking Information Exchange Standard Crosswalks with a Reasoner
entry.summary: From Certified Pairs to a Certified Hub: Reasoner-Checked Crosswalks for the Information Exchange Standard arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper addresses how digital twins in a national ecosystem are linked to a common foundation through mappings, and defines valid mappings as coherent and conservative when merged into one ontology. The authors test crosswalks from the Information Exchange Standard (IES) to thirteen ontologies, first pair by pair and then across whole hubs, using matching, human review, SKOS certification and the HermiT reasoner. Pairwise certification and review catch different errors, and together they make eleven of twelve overlapping pairs coherent and conservative. However, merging three building crosswalks made five Brick classes unsatisfiable, showing that pairwise certification does not compose and that the hub is the unit to certify.

entry.title: Real-time interactive world simulation with Cosmos for training physical AI
entry.summary: Interactive World Simulation with Cosmos for Physical AI arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper presents a shared framework that adapts Cosmos world foundation models for real-time interactive simulation. It streams visual observations in response to actions and scene controls, letting users and embodied agents interact with evolving virtual environments. The approach is demonstrated on camera navigation, robot manipulation, controllable video transfer, and multi-view autonomous vehicle simulation, with code and model checkpoints released.

entry.title: Learning to track cells in 3D microscopy videos using sparse labels
entry.summary: Learning to Track Cells from Sparse Annotations in 3D Time-Lapse Microscopy arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper presents a pipeline for tracking cells in 3D time-lapse microscopy, where only some cells are annotated, to reconstruct cell lineages. It detects cells from sparse annotations, calibrates candidate links using image features, and jointly selects lineage graph events. On 199 videos from 2 zebrafish embryos, it achieves an overall score of 0.9762 in 5-fold cross-validation.

entry.title: From Reconstruction to Imputation: Test-Time Optimization for Missing Time-Series Channels
entry.summary: From Reconstruction to Imputation: Test-Time Optimization for Missing Time-Series Channels arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper addresses time-series data loss from complete sensor-channel failures by converting a frozen reconstruction model into an imputer at inference time. For each test window, the missing entries are treated as optimization variables and refined by backpropagating through the frozen model, minimizing error only on observed values. Experiments on five real-world datasets show that this refinement often lowers error compared with one-pass reconstruction, but it requires much more inference time and is sensitive to cross-channel coupling.

entry.title: Alternatives to Shallow Autoencoders for Collaborative Filtering: Improving EASE with User-User Information
entry.summary: Alternatives to Shallow Autoencoders for Collaborative Filtering arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies EASE, a shallow autoencoder with a closed-form solution used for collaborative filtering in recommender systems. The authors argue that EASE relies mainly on item-item relationships, which may limit its ability to capture fine-grained similarities between users. They propose an alternative formulation based on EASE that uses user-user information, and a hybrid model combining user-user and item-item adjacency distributions. Experiments reported in the paper show that these models outperform EASE on well-known recommendation benchmarks.

entry.title: Verifier-Guided Self-Consistency: Improving LLM reasoning at test time
entry.summary: Verifier-Guided Self-Consistency: Test-Time Reasoning with Imperfect Generators and Verifiers arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies how to make large language models more accurate on multi-step reasoning problems during inference. The authors propose Verifier-Guided Self-Consistency (VGSC), which uses step-level correctness and future-outcome estimates from a verifier to guide generation while keeping multiple reasoning trajectories for final answer voting. The paper reports higher average accuracy than representative baselines across several reasoning benchmarks, generator models, and verifier families.

entry.title: Time-division multiplexing: a timing layer that schedules busy and idle operation for digital agents
entry.summary: Time-Division Multiplexing: The Operational Rhythm and Temporal Organization Layer of Digital Life arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper proposes a temporal organization layer that schedules a continual agent's online (busy) and offline (idle) operations as phases of one process. It gives a projected duty-cycle update with a deterministic descent guarantee and an extra noise term for a stochastic guarantee. Five synthetic experiments with 64 seeds each, plus a frozen-backbone Qwen3-8B prototype, test the design, and the authors state the results do not show machine consciousness or general agent superiority.

entry.title: Behavioral rate of fine-tuning: measuring useful information via compression
entry.summary: The Behavioral Rate of Fine-Tuning: Compression as a Measure of Useful Information arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper studies how much information LoRA fine-tuning must write, defining a behavioral rate R*: the smallest serialized size of a compressed adapter that, reloaded into a frozen base model, retains a fixed fraction of its held-out fine-tuning gain. Experiments show this rate rises with distinct training content and differs across frozen base models for the same dataset. Compressibility is thus a property of the dataset-receiver pair.

entry.title: A trust layer for fast pedestal-stability surrogates with error bars and alarms
entry.summary: A trust layer for fast pedestal-stability surrogates: calibrated error bars, out-of-distribution alarms and few-shot recalibration arXiv · Nov 4, 2026Machine-learning surrogates predict linear peeling-ballooning stability in milliseconds but usually give only point estimates. This paper proposes a model-agnostic trust layer combining conformal error bars, out-of-distribution alarms that send doubtful cases to the physics code, and recalibration from a few simulations of a new design. On JET-like equilibria and BOUT++ surrogates, the error bars keep nominal coverage in distribution but fall short under a plasma shape shift, and a few new-shape simulations or routing flagged cases restore it.

entry.title: SpikePose: A Lightweight Video Human Pose Estimator
entry.summary: SpikePose: Lightweight Video Human Pose Estimation arXiv · Nov 4, 2026SpikePose is a lightweight video human pose estimation method that combines a frame-reset, single-step spiking encoder with a motion-aligned heatmap memory (MAM). The encoder provides per-frame spatial evidence, while MAM estimates joint displacement, aligns historical heatmaps, and fuses them with current predictions. On MPII and an NTU60 subset, it reduces estimated arithmetic energy by 91.4% relative to an architecture-matched ANN with MAM, at a cost of 1.12 PCK_HB(0.5) points, and MAM lowers velocity and acceleration errors.

entry.title: BudgetSplat: A Budget-Controllable Generalizable Gaussian Splatting Method
entry.summary: BudgetSplat: Budget-Controllable Generalizable Gaussian Splatting arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper presents BudgetSplat, a feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting framework for novel view synthesis whose final representation size can be set by a user-specified preservation ratio. It addresses the problem that existing pixel-aligned methods generate highly redundant Gaussians, causing storage and rendering cost to grow quickly with resolution and input view count. Experiments on indoor reconstruction and cross-dataset generalization show consistent quality-size trade-offs across view counts and preservation ratios, with substantially reduced storage and rendering cost while preserving rendering quality.

entry.title: Finite-width shift of the edge of chaos in deep neural networks
entry.summary: Finite-width shift of the edge of chaos in deep neural networks arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper studies the "edge of chaos" used to initialise deep neural networks, a critical line known for infinitely wide networks. The authors model the log distance between two inputs as a random walk and compute its drift and variance to order 1/N, deriving how the critical weight variance shifts at finite width. Simulations of the exact finite-width recursion confirm the shift. They propose an initialisation rule, Crinit, which places networks on this finite-width edge and reports better accuracy than standard rules on MNIST and Fashion-MNIST at width 64.

entry.title: Moving from fixed defaults to calibrated activation choices for long-term forecasting
entry.summary: From Fixed Defaults to Calibrated Activation Policies for Long-Term Time-Series Forecasting arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies how activation function choices affect long-term time-series forecasting accuracy. The authors propose a calibrated selection policy that learns a reliable default from prior experiments, adapts the activation function and its placement to each task, and keeps the default when evidence for change is weak. Across 1,225 Informer training runs covering 51 forecasting tasks on 17 dataset variants, the policy reduced mean squared error by 7.86% on average versus a fixed-activation baseline and improved 72.55% of tasks.

entry.title: LungMend: a healthy-only diffusion model that corrects lung masks in severe TB CT scans
entry.summary: LungMend: A Healthy-Only Latent Diffusion Shape Prior for Lung Mask Correction in Severe Tuberculosis CT arXiv · Nov 4, 2026Standard lung segmentation models such as R231 often leave cavities and consolidations out of the lung mask in severe tuberculosis CT scans. LungMend is a post-processing model that corrects these masks using only healthy anatomy. Trained on healthy lungs with synthetically corrupted masks, it recovers the complete lung from the faulty mask and bone anatomy, without pathological data or CT intensities.

entry.title: RAGAM-AI: A hybrid reinforcement learning and generative AI agent approach for edge resource management
entry.summary: RAGAM-AI: A Hybrid Reinforcement Learning based Agentic approach powered by Generative AI for Edge Resource Management arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper proposes RAGAM-AI, a framework that combines reinforcement learning with generative AI to optimize resource allocation at multi-access edge computing (MEC) units. It uses a large language model to provide feedback that addresses reward generalization, and implements a multi-agent soft actor-critic (MASAC) method with Mathστral as the reward oracle. Compared with single-agent SAC, REINFORCE, and random policies, the approach reports lower CPU, memory, and bandwidth allocation deviations along with reduced latency and data rate costs.

entry.title: Adapting Sleep Foundation Models for Precise Sleep Spindle Localization
entry.summary: Adapting Sleep Foundation Models for Dense Sleep Spindle Localization arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies how to adapt a sleep foundation model to locate dense EEG events, focusing on the precise boundaries of sleep spindles. The authors freeze a pretrained SleepFM encoder and add a local time-frequency pathway that keeps spindle-relevant spectral content and intra-token position, while residual cross-attention brings in SleepFM's temporal context. On the MODA dataset, the model reaches an event-level F1 of 0.8080 ± 0.0040 at IoU 0.2 across six folds. Ablations indicate that localization depends mainly on local spectral and sub-token temporal information.

entry.title: When Summaries Turn Into Instructions: Unsupported Permissions in LLM Agents' Self-Written Handoff Notes
entry.summary: When Do Summaries Become Instructions? Unsupported Policy in LLM Agents' Self-Written Handoff Summaries arXiv · Nov 4, 2026Long-running LLM agents compress their context by replacing most history with a summary. This paper tests whether these handoff summaries state permissions or requirements the record does not support, whether such sentences change how the next agent behaves, and where they originate. In two open-weight models, about 1.2% and 2.4% of readable summaries contained unsupported restrictions, and about 0.1% and 1.3% contained unsupported authorizations. Neutralizing false approval sentences reduced unauthorized actions from 24 to 7 of 120 held-out runs (post hoc analysis).

entry.title: MKD2World: A Typed Spatial Markdown World Model for Web Agents
entry.summary: MKD2World: A Typed Spatial MarkDown World Model For Web Agents arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper introduces Typed Spatial Markdown (TSM), a Markdown-style text format that serializes desktop web interface elements by their spatial layout, types, and locations. It also presents AtomBlock-WebUI, a dataset used to train a screenshot-to-TSM renderer. Building on TSM, the authors propose MKD2World, a world model that describes current states and predicts next states given actions, and report improved web agent success rates on Online-Mind2Web.

entry.title: Reusing Experience Through Process Rubrics for Token-Level Credit in Agent Training
entry.summary: Using Experience Twice: Dynamic Process Rubrics for Privileged Token-Level Credit Assignment arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper addresses how agents trained with sparse trajectory-level rewards struggle to tell which key decisions to reinforce or suppress. It proposes Online Rubric Self-Distillation (ORSD), in which the current policy generates natural-language process rubrics from behavioral differences across a group of trajectories, and a frozen verifier selects the bundle best aligned with task success. The selected rubric is used as privileged information, and the log-likelihood gap with and without it provides per-token process credit added to the GRPO advantage. Experiments on ALFWorld and WebShop report faster policy improvement and higher final task performance for Qwen3-1.7B and Qwen3-4B under the same interaction budget.

entry.title: Controllable Multimodal Glioblastoma MRI Synthesis Using Latent Diffusion
entry.summary: Spatially and Compositionally Controlled Multimodal Glioblastoma MRI Synthesis with Latent Diffusion arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper proposes a two-stage latent diffusion model framework for generating 2D glioblastoma MRI scans whose tumour location, spatial extent, axial position, and subregion composition can be explicitly controlled. The first stage generates tumour segmentation maps, and the second stage uses ControlNet to produce T1, T1Gd, T2, and FLAIR images that follow the requested segmentation. On a held-out test set, the generated segmentations had a mean centroid error of 0.842 pixels, and ControlNet reduced pooled FID across the four modalities from 42.59 to 36.12. An expert reader study gave mean quality ratings of 6.60 for real images, 6.83 for ControlNet-generated images, and 6.77 for fully synthetic images.

entry.title: From Admission to Retention: Predicting Durable Offspring in Quality-Diversity Search
entry.summary: From Admission to Retention: Predicting Durable Offspring in Quality-Diversity Search arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies how to tell which offspring in an unstructured Quality-Diversity archive will stay in the archive generations later, using signals available before they reproduce. Experiments on a planar-arm benchmark and two robotic-locomotion tasks show that the same signals often point in opposite directions for entry and persistence. Lineage depth is the clearest signal, and its ability to separate persistent offspring grows with population capacity. However, biasing parent selection toward the strongest survival-linked signals did not improve search performance.

entry.title: IDSISA: a method for efficient machine unlearning that removes specific training data's influence.
entry.summary: IDSISA: Influence-Distilled Sharded Training for Efficient Machine Unlearning arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper introduces IDSISA (Influence-Distilled SISA), a machine unlearning method that removes the effect of specific training examples to meet privacy rules. It uses influence functions to group likely-to-be-forgotten samples into a few shards and applies distillation from unaffected shards to recover utility lost by isolated retraining. The authors also show that a cascading retraining procedure keeps the deletion guarantee for the full model under repeated deletion requests. Experiments on several architectures and datasets report better selective forgetting and utility retention than SISA, with unlearning-time changes from -6.7% to +6.4%.

entry.title: EmoReward: Self-Evolving Reward Calibration for Training Emotional Video Generation with Reinforcement Learning
entry.summary: EmoReward: Self-Evolving Reward Calibration for Emotional Video Generation RL arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper presents EmoReward, a self-evolving training method for reinforcement learning in emotional video generation. It estimates the reliability of different reward signals from reward traces gathered during a training run and uses these estimates to adjust multi-reward weights in later training. Experiments on HunyuanVideo 1.5 compare it with other agentic reward methods, with ablations and transfer tests on SD 3.5 and FLUX.

entry.title: Dialect Matters: A Dialect-Aware Baseline for Igala-English Machine Translation
entry.summary: Dialect Matters: A Dialect-Aware Baseline for Igala-English Machine Translation arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper presents a dialect-aware baseline for machine translation between Igala and English, among the first open systems for this language and the first to analyze dialectal variation. The dataset of 1,137 sentences is tagged by dialect, with Idah making up 40.4% and Ankpa 26.1%. A model trained on mixed dialects reaches a BLEU score of 11.66, while an Idah-only model scores 4.7 BLEU lower on Ibaji.

entry.title: A decision framework for acquiring failed banks that accounts for how risk factors interact, tested on FDIC deals
entry.summary: An Interaction-Aware Decision Framework for FDIC-Assisted Distressed Bank Acquisitions: Empirical Evidence from the FDIC Failed-Bank Panel and the SVB-First Citizens Case arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper proposes a Spider Network Filtering framework that links five dimensions through four interpretable interaction rules, producing features for a logistic model and a Pursue/Caution/Avoid decision rule for distressed bank acquisitions. It evaluates 55 FDIC-assisted acquisitions from 2008 to 2024 by U.S.-listed acquirers, using the three-day abnormal return around announcement as the market's initial reception. The Spider-enhanced model reaches a mean AUC of 0.594, below logistic regression (0.615) and ridge regression (0.632) on the same inputs.

entry.title: Predicting future model accuracy to prune weaker candidates during neural network training
entry.summary: Nowcasting Future Performance for Population Pruning in Survival-of-the-Fittest Training arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper investigates whether intermediate training checkpoints can predict a model's future accuracy, enabling more informed decisions about which candidate networks to stop early. The authors train nowcasters that take accuracy and loss histories, weight statistics, and SANE representations (a transformer autoencoder that encodes checkpoints as latent tokens) to predict test accuracy five epochs ahead or at the end of training. Weight statistics perform best for five-epoch forecasts, while SANE representations perform best for final accuracy. In model zoos with wide performance spread, such as ResNet-18 and ViT, Survival-of-the-Fittest training using predicted final accuracy nearly closes the gap to the best model.

entry.title: ElecLoad: Adaptive Electricity Load Forecasting Guided by Multiple Events
entry.summary: ElecLoad: Adaptive Electricity Load Forecasting Guided by Multiple Events arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper introduces ElecLoad, a context-aware agent for forecasting electricity load affected by multiple events. It combines historical load with event context to analyze each event's relevance, timing, and interactions. Based on this analysis, it either forecasts the whole horizon directly or partitions it into segments, with sub-agents producing and refining forecasts under a main agent's review. Experiments on multiple electricity load datasets show state-of-the-art performance in most scenarios.

entry.title: NaijaFacts: A Benchmark Separating Language Skill from Knowledge of Nigerian Facts
entry.summary: NaijaFacts: A Framework for Disentangling Language from Knowledge in Facts about Nigeria arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper introduces NaijaFacts, a benchmark of factual and statistical questions about Nigeria, written by native speakers and grounded in official statistics, and available in English, Nigerian Pidgin, Yoruba, Igbo, and Hausa. By comparing against similar questions about the UK and US, it separates a language effect from a knowledge effect. The knowledge effect dominates: English-query accuracy is 20% for Nigeria versus 49–50% for the US and UK, and no model exceeds 31% on Nigerian statistics. The authors report the same pattern across all 54 African countries.

entry.title: CRESiST: A Self-Improving Exploratory Learning Method for Real-Time Speech Translation
entry.summary: CRESiST: Self-Enhancing Explorative Policy Learning for Simultaneous Speech Translation arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper proposes an end-to-end read-write framework built on an omni-modal large language model that interleaves speech chunks and text tokens, enabling full KV cache reuse and segmentation-free, infinite-length inference. It introduces an Actor-Critic pipeline in which an RNN-T actor samples read-write trajectories and an LLM-based critic scores them using semantic and latency rewards, distilling the best policy back to the actor. Experiments on sentence-level and document-level benchmarks report new state-of-the-art quality-latency Pareto frontiers over cascaded and static-alignment baselines.

entry.title: Tools Need Not Speak in Text: Latent Context Compression for Agents
entry.summary: Tools Need Not Speak in Text: Latent Context Compression for Agents arXiv · Nov 4, 2026LLM agents usually append raw tool outputs to their context, where long, noisy observations add overhead and distract from task-relevant information. The paper proposes Coca-Cola, a model that compresses tool observations into latent tokens embedded in the agent's input space, trained with Action-Preserving Training so the agent's next-action distributions match under full and compressed observations. In experiments with web-search agents on four QA benchmarks and two model families, it reduces token consumption by 70.01%-89.24% and end-to-end runtime by 24.45%-55.97%, while consistently improving task performance.

entry.title: LibriSpeech-Real-QA: A Streaming Speech Question-Answering Benchmark
entry.summary: LibriSpeech-Real-QA: A Benchmark for Streaming Question Answering arXiv · Nov 4, 2026Most speech large language models still respond only after receiving a complete speech segment, although many applications need answers while audio is still arriving. The authors build LibriSpeech-Real-QA, a dataset and benchmark that tests whether models can identify target words in streaming audio. Evaluation of several commercial real-time models shows they still tend to respond only after the speech turn ends. The paper also shows that a pretrained speech model can be adapted to the task and establishes a baseline.

entry.title: FPTR: A feasibility-preserving method for joint beam and resource allocation under deadlines
entry.summary: FPTR: Feasibility-Preserving Transactional Refinement for Deadline-Constrained Joint Beam and Resource Allocation arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper addresses short-interval wireless schedulers that must output a complete, feasible beam and resource allocation before each deadline. It proposes Feasibility-Preserving Transactional Refinement (FPTR), which always keeps a validated feasible allocation and accepts a refined candidate only if it is complete, passes validation before its stage cutoff, and strictly improves the objective. On 150 synthetic instances, the full pipeline raises traffic by 3.83% on average over a lightweight beam-first reference.

entry.title: Evaluating small-data astronomical image classifiers independent of object identity
entry.summary: Object-independent evaluation of small-data astronomical image classifiers: architecture, representation, and acquisition shortcuts arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper introduces a dataset of 370 catalogue-supported astronomical objects across four classes (galaxies, globular clusters, nebulae, open clusters), each shown in three Digitised Sky Survey bands. It compares a custom CNN-Transformer trained from scratch with pretrained ResNet-50 and ViT-B/16 under several field-of-view and central-masking controls. Models generalise to unseen objects, but acquisition settings, image context, and catalogue-derived properties also carry substantial class information, so high accuracy does not show that morphology was learned.

entry.title: What multi-turn reinforcement learning actually improves in LLM agents
entry.summary: What Does Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning Really Improve in LLM Agents? arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper examines how multi-turn agentic reinforcement learning affects large language model agents. Using a Pass@(K,T) metric across sampling breadth K and interaction depth T, the authors find that RL's advantages depend on sufficient turn budgets and shrink when budgets tighten. They also introduce BudgetMix RL, which varies interaction budgets during training, and report robust performance across diverse execution settings.

entry.title: ArcRAG: Agentic retrieval over knowledge graphs that works across different graph builds
entry.summary: ArcRAG: Agentic Compositional Retrieval over Knowledge Graphs arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper introduces ArcRAG, a graph-based retrieval method that, at inference time, builds a query-specific graph interface from the entities a question names, then plans and executes multi-hop searches as Cypher queries. The authors test it on MuSiQue, HotpotQA, and TriviaQA, each built as both a schema-guided graph and an open-information-extraction graph. They find that a construction-agnostic retriever stays effective when the graph construction changes, though construction still affects absolute accuracy.

entry.title: Uncertainty-guided surrogate enhancement and inverse design for microdroplet generators
entry.summary: Microdroplet Generator Surrogate Enhancement and Inverse Design Through an Uncertainty-Guided Framework arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper proposes a method that combines adaptive surrogate enhancement with simulation-driven inverse design for microfluidic droplet generators. Volume-of-Fluid simulations provide ground-truth data, and neural network ensembles predict flow regimes and droplet diameters, with uncertainty concentrated near regime transition boundaries. Targeted additional simulations in these regions and retraining improve the ensembles, and Particle Swarm Optimization is used for constrained inverse design. Validation shows higher accuracy, with the share of diameter predictions within 0-3% error nearly doubling, and reliable identification of physically realizable configurations meeting target droplet sizes.

entry.title: CoDecide: Content-Adaptive Video Decoding for Fast Video Analytics
entry.summary: CoDecide: Content-Adaptive Video Decoding for High-Throughput Video Analytics arXiv · Nov 4, 2026CoDecide is a retrospective video analytics system that decodes only the frames where new content appears, using signals from the compressed video bitstream. It trains a lightweight compressed-domain model on a label-free novelty signal from a frozen DINOv2 teacher, so it generalizes to new cameras without per-camera retraining. Detections from decoded frames are propagated to skipped frames using motion vectors. Evaluated on VIRAT, MEVA, and ShanghaiTech, it recovers more moving-object detections than prior compressed-domain selectors at the same decoding budget and runs 15 to 24 times faster than decoding and detecting every frame.

entry.title: Failure-boundary profiles for closed-loop testing of driving and robot navigation agents
entry.summary: Beyond Infraction Scores: Failure-Boundary Profiles for Closed-Loop Evaluation of Driving and Robot Navigation Agents arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper argues that the CARLA driving score cannot tell an agent that stops before an obstacle from one that pushes past it. It proposes failure-boundary profiles, in which scenario families vary one measured factor such as corridor width or oncoming-traffic gap, and each variant is labeled as proceed or stop. For each agent it estimates commitment and competence curves and the points where they cross one half, along with a decision-accuracy metric. Seven driving agents on seven CARLA families are evaluated, and the same method is applied to a warehouse robot navigation policy in Isaac Sim.

entry.title: EfficientNet Model-Size Scaling for Retinal Disease Classification from OCT Scans
entry.summary: Within-Family EfficientNet Scaling under Fixed-Resolution Transfer Learning for Spectral-Domain Optical Coherence Tomography Retinal Disease Classification arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This study tests EfficientNet-B0 through B7, pretrained on ImageNet, at a fixed 224x224 resolution for four-class classification of retinal diseases from spectral-domain OCT images in the Kermany dataset. Accuracy did not rise steadily with model size: B1 scored highest at 96.95%, while B7 reached 96.73%. The authors conclude that larger variants did not consistently improve results, so scaling effects depend on the task and protocol. Results are conditional on the supplied data split.

entry.title: AmbiHTMLBench: A Benchmark for Parsing Visually Rich Documents into HTML
entry.summary: AmbiHTMLBench: A Benchmark for HTML-based Visually Rich Document parsing arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper introduces AmbiHTMLBench, a benchmark where models must convert real-world documents into executable HTML that preserves content, organization, and visual appearance. It contains 1,115 diverse pages and evaluates results both objectively, through table fidelity, text error, and layout consistency, and subjectively, through LLM judges aligned with human preferences. Across ten multimodal systems, the best objective score is 0.8092, and the top subjective system differs from it. The authors also report that fine-tuning a small expert model performs well on document-to-HTML reconstruction.

entry.title: SUMONE: A Simple, Efficient Plug-and-Play Summarizer for Agent Memory
entry.summary: SUMONE: A Simple and Efficient Summarizer for Plug-and-Play Agent Memory arXiv · Nov 4, 2026SumOne is a standalone summarizer that compresses long interaction histories of language-model agents. It is trained through masked reconstruction, so it needs no reference summaries or downstream task execution. Only the lightweight summarizer is kept at inference, allowing it to plug into existing agents without changes. On DeepSearchQA and SWE-bench Verified, the paper reports about 78% and 75% lower estimated inference cost, with an absolute accuracy decrease of 0.04.

entry.title: EvoGuard: Preventing Performance Decline as Agent Skills Evolve Online
entry.summary: EvoGuard: Mitigating Degradation in Online Skill Evolution arXiv · Nov 4, 2026Language agents can store experience as natural-language skill documents, but skills updated online may degrade performance. EvoGuard is a pairwise selector trained on utility labels from private test sets to choose the better of two skills. At deployment it makes its decision in a single forward pass, much faster than full evaluation. It improves success over adopting every new skill by 11.0% on ALFWorld, 5.9% on ScienceWorld, and 2.7% on LiveCodeBench.

entry.title: Pretrained graph models adapted to detect anomalies in multivariate time series
entry.summary: Graph Foundation Models Can Become Effective Multivariate Time Series Anomaly Detectors arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper introduces Gfm4Mtsad, a framework that adapts pretrained Graph Foundation Models to multivariate time series anomaly detection. It includes modules for aligning time series with the pretrained graph space, generating pseudo-anomalies for supervision, and calibrating scores when aggregating from nodes to windows. Experiments with two graph foundation model backbones reportedly show better detection performance than existing baselines.
